However, the electroclinical features of seizures and anti-seizure medication (ASM) responses in this subtype remain poorly characterized. We report a 10-month-old female infant presenting with the classic ECCL triad: nevus psiloliparus, ocular choristoma, and right cerebral hemispheric dysplasia. She developed frequent epileptic spasms starting at 3 months of age, consistent with a Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy (DEE). Video-EEG captured focal-onset spasms with right-hemisphere-predominant electrographic abnormalities. The patient exhibited a suboptimal response to a prolonged trial of first-line hormonal therapy (2-week ACTH followed by a 3-month oral prednisone taper) and subsequent multiple antiseizure medications (ASMs), fulfilling the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) criteria for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy (DRE). High-depth whole-exome sequencing (mean depth 150.85×) of the lesional skin tissue confirmed a somatic mosaic KRAS c.35G > A (p.Gly12Asp) mutation (variant allele frequency [VAF] of 19%), while peripheral blood testing was negative. This case expands the electroclinical phenotype of KRAS-related ECCL to include focal-onset epileptic spasms within a DEE framework. It highlights a critical diagnostic pitfall: low systemic mosaic burden frequently leads to false-negative peripheral blood genetic tests. Therefore, high-depth sequencing of affected lesional tissue is mandatory for definitive diagnosis when clinical suspicion remains high.

papers.title: Diagnostic misclassification in suspected new-onset seizures: a prospective study of non-epileptic paroxysmal events and age-dependent patterns.
papers.abstract: Paroxysmal events resembling epileptic seizures frequently lead to diagnostic error and unnecessary treatment exposure. While non-epileptic paroxysmal events (NEPE) are recognized as common seizure mimics, the age-dependent structure of the differential diagnosis and patterns of antiseizure medication (ASM) exposure remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a prospective national referral cohort study of consecutive patients referred for evaluation of suspected new-onset seizures. All patients underwent standardized clinical assessment, video-electroencephalography, and longitudinal follow-up. NEPE were classified into five predefined diagnostic subgroups, and multinomial logistic regression was used to model age-related diagnostic probabilities. Of 1,877 patients referred over 4 years, 428 (22.8%) were diagnosed with NEPE, including 305 pediatric and 123 adult cases. Syncope was the most frequent diagnosis (30.8%), followed by functional seizures (21.7%). Distinct age-dependent distributions of non-epileptic diagnoses emerged: infantile mimics (including breath-holding spells and Sandifer syndrome) predominated in early childhood, behavioral-movement phenomena peaked in childhood, functional seizures increased during adolescence and young adulthood, and syncope became progressively more prevalent with advancing age. Developmental delay was strongly associated with behavioral-movement diagnoses (OR 10.60, 95% CI 3.45-32.61). Pre-referral ASM exposure occurred in 102 patients (23.8%), with patients with functional seizures three times more likely to be treated before diagnostic clarification than those with syncope (adjusted OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.47-6.46). NEPE follow predictable age-related distributions that may guide early clinical assessment. The high rate of ASM exposure prior to diagnostic clarification, particularly in functional seizures, highlights the clinical consequences of early misdiagnosis. Incorporation of age-based clinical reasoning may improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce unnecessary treatment exposure in patients with paroxysmal events.

papers.title: Factors influencing sleep architecture following matches in elite male soccer players: a longitudinal squad case study.
papers.abstract: This study explored the effects of various situational match day factors on subsequent sleep quantity and architecture in elite male soccer players; we hypothesized that kick off (KO) time and next day schedule would have the greatest impact on sleep. Sleep was recorded following 134 matches using wrist worn WHOOP bands (Whoop, Inc., Boston, MA, USA) in 15 male professional soccer players (age 26±4 years) competing in the English Premier League (EPL). Total sleep time (TST), sleep efficiency (SE), deep sleep, rapid eye movement (REM), light sleep, sleep disturbances, and wake time were measured after 512 sleep nights. A linear mixed model with random coefficients examined the impact of the following variables on sleep: player age, match location (home vs. away), KO time (<1700h vs. ≥1700h), match outcome (win, draw, loss), quality of opposition, minutes played, sprint distance and next day context (training or rest day). TST was shortened by later KO times (unstandardized regression coefficient [B]=-69.5; P<0.001), after playing top vs. bottom tier teams (B=-26.5; P=0.005), and affected by match outcome and increased sprint distance (all P<0.05). KO time and sprint distance were significant predictors of sleep disturbances (all P<0.05); KO time and playing time (P<0.001) were significant predictors of REM and light sleep. Other than mildly reducing sleep disturbances (B=-0.8; P=0.021), a training day did not influence sleep. In professional male soccer players, later KO times had the biggest impact on sleep indices following matches, while scheduling a rest or training day after matches did not influence sleep duration or architecture, despite a minor change in sleep disturbances.
papers.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness

papers.title: Integrating bioethnography into sleep research: generating better measures, hypotheses, and interpretations.
papers.abstract: Sleep research increasingly uses actigraphy, biomarkers, and structured surveys to quantify sleep duration and quality across populations. Yet researchers often interpret these measures without sufficient attention to the social, relational, and structural contexts surrounding sleep. This report presents bioethnography as a complementary methodological approach integrating sustained ethnographic engagement with epidemiological research. The report situates bioethnography alongside developmental-cultural, social-ecological, biocultural, and clinically oriented ecological approaches to sleep and identifies bioethnography's specific contribution: an iterative research architecture allowing ethnographic findings to reshape hypotheses, measurements, analyses, and interpretations of biological data. Drawing on a bioethnographic study of sleep among midlife women enrolled in a long-standing cohort in Mexico City, the report demonstrates how open-ended inquiry generates new hypotheses, reveals unmeasured social processes shaping sleep, and refines the interpretation of quantitative sleep metrics. By situating biological data within lived experience, bioethnography produces 'better numbers': more valid, interpretable findings responsive to population-specific realities. The report discusses the approach's strengths and limitations and outlines practical strategies for integrating bioethnography into sleep research. Bioethnography does not replace established ecological or biosocial frameworks; rather, the approach offers a way to operationalize a shared commitment to understanding sleep as a biological process embedded in social life.

papers.title: Interpreting sarcoidosis global fatigue endpoints: associations of depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance in an observational study.
papers.abstract: Fatigue in sarcoidosis is common and burdensome, reflecting multiple co-occurring symptom domains, yet trials often treat fatigue as a single endpoint. To examine the associations between depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, and fatigue endpoints. We analyzed two US sarcoidosis cohorts that completed Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Fatigue, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) for depressive symptoms, and the General Sleep Disturbance Scale (GSDS). Scores were standardized. Cohort-stratified and pooled linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and race estimated associations of depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance with fatigue. Model R2 values were compared across single-predictor and multivariable models. Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for lung function and immunosuppressive therapy and substituted a modified PHQ-9 score (ie, PHQ-9 excluding the fatigue item). Among 120 University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), and 104 Risk Indicators of Sarcoidosis Evolution-Unified Protocol Study (RISE-UP) participants, depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance were associated with fatigue. In single-predictor models, a 1-SD increase in PHQ-9 and GSDS scores was associated with higher fatigue scores, with mean differences of 0.78 and 0.79 in UCSF and 0.50 and 0.52 in RISE-UP, respectively. In multivariable models including both predictors, depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance remained independently associated with fatigue, and explained variance was high (R2 = 0.76 in UCSF and R2 = 0.40 in RISE-UP; pooled R2 = 0.62). Demographic characteristics contributed minimally. Sensitivity analyses adjusting for lung function and immunosuppression and using the modified PHQ-9 yielded similar results. Depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance explain a substantial proportion of fatigue score variability in sarcoidosis, underscoring the need for multidimensional outcome measures in clinical trials. NCT05567133.
papers.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

papers.title: Occupational Perspectives on Sleep Health in High-Demand Occupations: A PEOP-Informed Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Sleep deficiency is prevalent in military and comparable high-demand occupations and contributes to fatigue, impaired cognitive functioning, occupational performance deficits, and operational risk. This scoping review synthesized occupation-relevant, nonpharmacological sleep interventions for adults in high-demand occupations and examined implications for sleep participation, occupational performance, and occupational therapy practice. Scopus, PubMed, and PsycINFO were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between February 2015 and May 2026. Thirty-seven studies met inclusion criteria and were synthesized using the Person-Environment-Occupation-Performance model. Person-level interventions most consistently improved subjective sleep quality, insomnia symptoms, stress regulation, and perceived recovery, whereas objective physiologic sleep outcomes were less consistent. Environment- and occupation-level interventions influenced sleep continuity, circadian alignment, fatigue mitigation, morale, and occupational performance when aligned with operational schedules and recovery opportunities. Multilevel interventions demonstrated the strongest cross-domain improvements. Findings support occupation-centered, systems-level approaches to sleep health in high-demand occupational settings.

papers.title: Impact of Ambient Temperature on PAP Adherence: A Retrospective Analysis of a Prospective OSA Cohort.
papers.abstract: Early adherence failure is a major driver of positive airway pressure (PAP) discontinuation in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Although seasonal variation in PAP use has been reported, the relationship between environmental conditions at treatment initiation and clinically defined early adherence remains incompletely understood. This study evaluated whether ambient temperature at PAP initiation was associated with subsequent PAP adherence and compared its relative contribution with conventional baseline clinical factors. This retrospective analysis used a prospectively enrolled OSA cohort. Overall, 342 adults who initiated auto-adjusting PAP therapy between 2018 and 2024 were included. Adherence was defined according to Korean national insurance criteria as PAP use for ≥4 hours per night on ≥70% of nights during any consecutive 28-day period within the first 3 months. Ambient temperature at PAP initiation was obtained from national meteorological data. Hierarchical logistic regression was performed using variables available at or before PAP initiation. A logistic regression-based SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework with repeated stratified cross-validation was used to compare relative feature contributions, and a feature-ablation analysis was used to evaluate the contributions of temperature and baseline AHI to model discrimination. Among 342 patients, 238 (69.6%) met adherence criteria. Adherence was lower in patients initiating PAP during May-September than during October- April (61.7% vs. 75.1%, P=0.008). In the fully adjusted baseline model (n=334), higher monthly mean daily maximum temperature was associated with lower odds of adherence (OR, 0.95 per 1°C increase; 95% CI, 0.92- 0.98; P=0.001). Higher temperature was also associated with shorter average daily PAP use at 3 months in a secondary analysis. The crossvalidated logistic model showed modest discrimination (AUROC, 0.653± 0.059). Within this model, temperature showed the largest mean absolute SHAP value, followed by baseline AHI. Excluding temperature or baseline AHI reduced the AUROC to a similar extent (0.029 for both), indicating comparable contributions to discrimination. Higher ambient temperature at PAP initiation was associated with lower early PAP adherence and contributed to model discrimination to a degree comparable to that of baseline OSA severity. Patients initiating PAP during warmer periods, particularly summer, may warrant closer early follow-up and additional support to facilitate PAP adaptation and adherence.

papers.title: Self-Management Program for Fatigue: Effects on Sleep, Resilience, and Occupational Balance-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is a common issue that can significantly impact the daily lives of university students. The aim of this study is to examine the effectiveness of a self-management program (SMP) on fatigue, sleep quality, resilience, and occupational balance in university students experiencing high levels of fatigue. Fifty-one students participated in, and completed, the study, including 26 in the intervention group and 25 in the control group. Participants aged 18 and above who scored 4 or higher on the Piper Fatigue Scale and reported no known diagnosed health condition that could independently contribute to fatigue were included in the study. Intervention group participated in a structured SMP lasting 12 weeks. The Piper Fatigue Scale, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality index, the Psychological Resilience Scale for Adults, and the Occupational Balance Questionnaire were used for assessment. Post-intervention analyses revealed that the intervention group exhibited improvements in fatigue, sleep quality, and occupational balance (p < .05). No significant between-group difference was found in psychological resilience (p > .05). SMP can be an effective option at universities to reduce fatigue, improve sleep patterns, and enhance well-being through better balance in daily activities.

papers.title: AI-assisted development of a rule-based pipeline for pre-examination screening in clinical neuropsychology: An exploratory method-development study.
papers.abstract: We present an exploratory, method-development study of a framework for rule-based pre-examination screening. The study is exploratory: no clinical endpoint, success threshold, or control condition was pre-specified. Demonstrated on retrospectively analyzed irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) data, the pipeline produces a structured analysis with cross-domain pattern detection and audience-tailored reports. A large language model was used as a coding assistant to draft scoring logic, cross-domain rules, and Python code. The deployed pipeline executes these fixed rules deterministically; no model inference occurs when patient data are processed. The pipeline processes five instruments (Bergen Insomnia Scale, Conners' Continuous Performance Test, Chalder Fatigue Scale, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, and the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status). For each patient, it generates an eight-step processing sequence, visualizations, and clinician-gated reports. Analyses used data from 105 adults (65 IBS, 40 controls) from the Bergen Brain-Gut-Microbiota study. The tool flagged findings above threshold in sleep (50%), fatigue (40%), anxiety (35%), and attention (30%), with multi-domain flags in 60%. Cross-domain rules linked co-occurring findings to candidate mechanisms drawn from published literature. Two case illustrations demonstrated the rule-based summaries alongside clinician interpretation that went beyond the rules. The framework is a transparent support tool rather than an autonomous reasoning system: every output traces to a stated rule, and the contribution of artificial intelligence lies in development, not deployment: it augments rather than replaces clinical judgment. Because the analysis is exploratory and single-cohort, the findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective, comparative validation.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society : JINS

papers.title: Association Between Hospital Performance and Care Delivery for out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
papers.abstract: IntroductionOut-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a leading cause of death worldwide, with substantial variation in survival between hospitals. Differences in post-arrest hospital care may explain this variation. We used a US national claims database to evaluate the association between increasing hospital performance and provision of care interventions.MethodsWe retrospectively studied the 2020-2022 National Emergency Department Sample database. OHCAs were defined by emergency department visits with: (1) an ICD-10 cardiac arrest diagnosis; or, (2) procedure codes for cardiopulmonary resuscitation. We included adult (age >18) patients with an associated hospitalization, excluding ED visits with a disposition of death. The main outcome was provision of hospital care interventions. Hospital performance quartiles were primarily defined by each hospital's proportion of OHCA patients surviving to hospital discharge. Using ordinal logistic regression, we evaluated the association between increasing hospital performance quartile and care intervention, accounting for patient demographics and year of cardiac arrest.ResultsAmong 192,207 patients treated at 1565 hospitals, survival to discharge was higher at top-quartile hospitals than bottom-quartile hospitals (46.0% vs 24.4%). Interventional cardiac procedures were associated with increasing hospital performance (left heart catheterization-aOR 2.0[1.8-2.1]; percutaneous coronary intervention-aOR 1.9[1.8-2.0]; ventricular assist device-aOR 1.8[1.7-2.0]; automatic implantable cardioverter defibrillator-aOR 2.2[2.1-2.4]; extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-aOR 3.3[2.4-4.5]; coronary artery bypass graft-aOR 2.4[2.1-2.7]). Arterial line placement (aOR 1.2[1.04-1.4]) and therapeutic hypothermia (aOR 1.5[1.1-2.3]) were also associated with increasing hospital performance quartile. Other interventions were not associated or were inversely associated with hospital performance: echocardiography, body imaging, head imaging, electroencephalogram, central lines, do not resuscitate orders.ConclusionInterventional cardiac procedures were consistently associated with increasing hospital performance quartile; arterial line placement and therapeutic hypothermia were associated only in our primary analysis. Diagnostic and neuroprognostication procedures were not associated with, or were inversely associated with, increasing hospital performance.

papers.title: Acceptability of Multiple Micronutrient Supplement Among Pregnant Women in the Philippines.
papers.abstract: The use of multiple micronutrient supplements (MMS) during pregnancy has been shown to reduce low birth weight, stillbirth, and preterm birth compared to iron-folic acid (IFA); however, evidence on user experiences and acceptability among pregnant women remains limited. This paper aimed to assess the acceptability of MMS among pregnant women in rural Philippines, focusing on sensory attributes, packaging preferences, and barriers to use. Data were drawn from two separate studies with non-overlapping samples: a 14-day Home Placement Test (HPT) involving 48 participants using MMS for the first time, followed by a prospective cohort survey of 971 participants. Participants in both studies completed acceptability surveys, rating MMS and its features on a 5-point hedonic scale. HPT participants also provided feedback through semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data from the two studies were analyzed separately. Participants mean age was 26 years in both HPT and cohort groups, and one-third were primiparous. In both studies, over 80% of respondents reported that they "liked very much" or "liked a little" the MMS. Median scores for sensory and packaging characteristics were 5, indicating high acceptability. Factors influencing its acceptability included the neutral taste, absence of metallic aftertaste or rusty smell, user-friendly blister packaging, and perceived improvements in appetite and sleep. Barriers included difficulty swallowing tablets, mild gastrointestinal discomfort, and limited awareness of MMS benefits. Tailored counseling, targeted messaging, and improvements to sensory features and packaging can help improve MMS acceptability, overcome barriers, and support the effective rollout of MMS in antenatal care programs within the Philippines.

papers.title: Interaction between 3-SNP genetic risk score and lifestyle risk score on cardiovascular risk factors and the risk of lifetime ASCVD among overweight and obese women.
papers.abstract: Interaction between genetic variations and lifestyle risk factors has been shown to be associated with atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD). This study for the first time sought to investigate this interaction on cardiovascular risk factors and the lifetime ASCVD risk in Iranian obese and overweight women. This study consisted of 256 overweight or obese women. The genetic risk score (GRS) included three genetic variations (CAV-1 rs3807992, CRY-1 rs2287161 and MC4R rs17782313), and each of them was genotyped using PCR-restriction fragment length polymorphism. Lifestyle risk score (LRS) consisting of dietary behaviour, physical activity, sleep quality, socio-economic status and waist-to-stature ratio was used to assess lifestyle risk factors associated with ASCVD, and the Bonferroni correction was also applied for multiple comparisons. Following Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons using a family-wise approach (α = 0·0028 for interaction analyses), the interaction between high LRS and high GRS was not significantly associated with any assessed cardiovascular risk factor or lifetime ASCVD risk. The nominal P-values for these interactions were 0·040 (CRI-II), 0·038 (CHOLINDEX), 0·018 (TyG-BMI), 0·041 (TAG), 0·041 (AIP), 0·067 (HDL), 0·075 (LDL) and 0·077 (ASCVD lifetime risk), all of which exceeded the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold. In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating study, uncorrected analyses suggested preliminary nominally significant interactions. However, after adjusting for multiple comparisons, no definitive evidence of GRS × LRS interactions was observed. These findings require replication in larger, prospective cohorts.

papers.title: The Undeniable Value of Sleep for Developmental Science.
papers.abstract: Sleep is a pervasive and fundamentally developmental phenomenon, yet its significance for behavioral and brain development remains underappreciated. Here, I argue that sleep is not merely influenced by developmental processes, nor simply supportive of them, but is itself a central, organizing principle of development. Within developmental systems theory, experience includes stimulation from both external and internal sources, including the spontaneous neural and motor activity that occurs during sleep. In early life, active (REM) sleep predominates and is accompanied by abundant myoclonic twitching, a source of discrete sensory input that cascades through the sensorimotor system to help establish and refine functional neural connections. Sleep also provides the physiological context for the emergence of organized brain rhythms and long-distance functional connectivity. In addition, sleep-wake states interact dynamically with physical and physiological factors-including thermoregulation-both shaping and being shaped by the infant's local environment. Finally, sleep modulates gene expression and supports the cellular mechanisms necessary for growth and plasticity. Together, these observations highlight sleep as an emergent property of developing systems that both reflects and drives neurobehavioral change. By incorporating sleep more fully into developmental analysis, we will better understand the nonlinear, context-dependent processes that underlie typical and atypical development.

papers.title: Plasma Metabolic Proteomics Links Phenoconversion and Disease-Specific Brain 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography Pattern Expressions in Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.abstract: Cellular metabolic dysfunction has emerged as a key contributor to neurodegeneration, but its role in Lewy body disease (LBD), particularly during prodromal stages, remains unclear. We investigated targeted blood-based proteomic profiles related to metabolic pathways across the REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD)-LBD continuum, and explored their potential as biomarkers of disease severity and phenoconversion. In this prospective cohort study, we enrolled 116 patients across the RBD-LBD continuum, including 47 with polysomnography-confirmed isolated RBD (iRBD), 45 with Parkinson's disease (PD) with RBD, and 24 with dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) with RBD, along with 30 age-matched healthy controls. Plasma concentrations of 92 metabolism-related proteins were measured using a proximity extension assay. Motor function, neuropsychological assessments, and brain 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography imaging were obtained. Patients with iRBD were prospectively followed for up to 4 years to monitor phenoconversion. Compared with controls, 16 differentially expressed metabolism-related proteins were identified across the RBD-LBD continuum, with predominant enrichment in neutrophil degranulation pathways. These protein alterations were mainly observed in patients with clinically manifest LBD, with DOPA decarboxylase demonstrating the most prominent differential expression and significant correlations with levodopa equivalent daily dose. In contrast, only N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) was significantly upregulated in patients with iRBD. Elevated NT-proBNP levels were associated with orthostatic intolerance, increased PD- and DLB-related metabolic brain pattern expressions, and earlier phenoconversion. Plasma metabolic proteins showed stage-specific alterations across the RBD-LBD continuum. NT-proBNP may have potential as a marker of short-term phenoconversion risk in iRBD. ANN NEUROL 2026.

papers.title: Circulating TIMP2 associates with brain health and lifestyle factors.
papers.abstract: Systemic tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 2 (TIMP2) can rejuvenate brain function in aged mice. We examined relevance in human brain aging and tested its modulation by pro-plasticity behaviors across humans and mice. Plasma TIMP2 was quantified via SomaScan in three human cohorts (University of California, San Francisco [UCSF]: n = 83; Stanford: n = 31; Religious Orders Study and Memory and Aging Project [ROSMAP]: n = 213). We examined TIMP2's associations with cognition, brain volume, and lifestyle behaviors. We then leveraged mouse models to establish links between environmental enrichment, circulating TIMP2, and adult hippocampal neurogenesis. Higher plasma TIMP2 associated with better global cognition and larger brain volumes across human cohorts. Physical activity and changes in multi-domain lifestyle factors positively associated with plasma TIMP2 in humans. Mice exposed to an enriched environment paradigm exhibited elevated plasma TIMP2, and environmental enrichment-mediated neurogenesis elevation was lost in mice lacking TIMP2. TIMP2 is clinically relevant to human brain aging and is associated with lifestyle-related neuroprotection.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

papers.title: Cannabidiol for chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with exploratory tetrahydrocannabinol add-on.
papers.abstract: Persistent chronic pain remains a major unmet need in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and ankylosing spondylitis (AS), even when inflammatory disease activity is low. Evidence for cannabinoid-based treatment in inflammatory rheumatic disease is limited. We investigated the efficacy and safety of low-dose cannabidiol (CBD) for chronic pain in RA and AS and explored the effects of adjunctive tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in non-responders. In this multicentre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 66 patients with RA or AS and persistent pain despite low inflammatory disease activity were randomized 1:1 to oral CBD or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was a reduction of at least 20 points on the pain visual analogue scale (VAS) at week 12. After the blinded phase, non-responders entered a 12-week open-label phase: non-responders in the placebo group switched to CBD, while non-responders in the CBD group received add-on THC. Secondary outcomes included continuous pain VAS, sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), cognitive performance assessed by the Trail Making Test (TMT) and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST), disease activity measures, and safety. At week 12, the primary endpoint was achieved by 9/32 patients (28%) receiving placebo and 3/30 patients (10%) receiving low-dose CBD. Low-dose CBD did not demonstrate superior pain relief compared with placebo and was associated with poorer sleep quality, while no significant between-group differences were observed for cognitive outcomes or inflammatory markers. In the exploratory open-label phase, 9/23 patients (39%) receiving CBD plus THC achieved the predefined pain response criterion compared with 2/25 patients (8%) receiving CBD alone. The CBD + THC group also showed greater improvements in continuous pain VAS and sleep quality. Low-dose CBD did not yield meaningful pain relief. The addition of low-dose THC was associated with improvements in pain and sleep quality. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in blinded randomized controlled trials. European Union Clinical Trials Register, EudraCT 2017-004226-15, prospectively registered before enrolment of the first participant; Danish Medicines Agency 2018-010018.

papers.title: The effects of psychoeducation-supported breathing and relaxation exercises on Post-Traumatic stress symptoms and sleep quality in earthquake survivors.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of psychoeducation-supported breathing and relaxation exercises on post-traumatic stress symptoms and sleep quality in individuals affected by the February 6, 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye. While such interventions have shown promise in various trauma-exposed populations, their specific impact on earthquake survivors remains underexplored. The study sought to determine whether a structured, low-cost group-based intervention could improve psychological recovery and sleep quality in this vulnerable group. A randomized controlled pre-test-post-test design was employed in this study. The population consisted of earthquake survivors residing in temporary shelters in Malatya, one of the provinces most severely affected by the February 6, 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye. A total of 203 earthquake survivors were assessed for eligibility; 90 participants were randomized equally into the intervention and control groups, and 84 completed the study and were included in the final analysis (42 in the intervention group and 42 in the control group). Data were collected using the sociodemographic form, the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Short Scale (PTSD-SS), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The intervention group received six sessions of psychoeducation-supported breathing and relaxation exercises delivered in a group training format. No intervention was provided to the control group. Following the intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in post-traumatic stress symptoms and sleep quality compared to the control group (p < .05). Specifically, the mean PTSD-SS score in the intervention group decreased by 5.45 points, and the mean PSQI score decreased by 3.88 points, indicating reduced post-traumatic stress symptoms and improved sleep quality. Breathing and relaxation exercises supported by psychoeducation appear to be a low-cost and effective approach for reducing post-traumatic stress symptoms and improving sleep quality among individuals affected by disasters. The integration of such interventions into post-disaster psychosocial support programs may contribute to the mental health and overall well-being of earthquake survivors. NCT07781904. Retrospectively registered on August 21, 2026.

papers.title: Cry2 linked silkworm domestication to highly synchronized eclosion and rhythmic head transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Domestication often enhances the temporal synchronization of life-history events; yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the circadian basis of domestication-associated synchronization by comparing eclosion rhythms and circadian transcriptomes between the domesticated silkworm (Bombyx mori) and its wild ancestor (B. mandarina), and functionally dissected the role of the clock gene Cry2. Under 14:10 light-dark cycles, both species exhibited significant daily eclosion rhythms; however, B. mori showed markedly higher synchronization and a distinct phase advance, resulting in a sharply clustered early-morning peak compared with the broader afternoon pattern in B. mandarina. Cry2 knockout did not substantially affect eclosion timing under LD cycles, but under constant darkness it delayed phase, reduced robustness and synchronization of the eclosion rhythm, suggesting that Cry2 promotes the precision and synchrony of endogenous eclosion rhythms. To uncover transcriptional signatures of domestication, we performed 24-h RNA-seq on heads of domestic, wild, and Cry2-mutant silkworms. Thousands of rhythmic genes and broad oscillatory expression of core clock genes were detected in B. mori, whereas only dozens of rhythmic transcripts were found in B. mandarina. Disruption of Cry2 strongly reduced the detectable domestication-expanded rhythmic transcriptional program, reducing the number of rhythmic genes from thousands to fewer than one hundred. Rhythmic outputs in B. mori were enriched in protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum, Toll/Imd signaling, and daytime-biased tyrosine metabolism/dopamine biosynthesis pathways. Co-expression network analysis further revealed that domestication strengthened clock-linked regulatory networks, which became fragmented in both the Cry2 mutant and wild silkworms. These findings demonstrate that domestication promotes interindividual synchronization of eclosion by expanding and coordinating circadian transcriptional programs, suggesting that Cry2 acts as a potential candidate gene contributing to this adaptive rhythmic network.

papers.title: Food insecurity and 24-hour movement behaviors in adolescents: associations with guideline adherence and behavioral combinations.
papers.abstract: Food insecurity is an important social determinant of health that may be associated with adolescents' daily movement behaviors. However, existing research has primarily focused on individual behaviors, with limited attention to adherence to integrated 24-hour movement guidelines and their behavioral combinations. This study examined the associations between food insecurity and adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines, as well as specific combinations of movement behaviors among adolescents. Data were drawn from the 2019 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS), a large sample of 45,571 students in grades 9-12. Multinomial logistic regression models were used to examine the associations between food insecurity and (1) the number of 24-hour movement guidelines met and (2) specific combinations of movement behaviors. Adolescents who met none of the guidelines were treated as the reference group. Results are presented as relative risk ratios (RRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for covariates. Overall, food insecurity was associated with a lower likelihood of meeting the 24-hour movement guidelines, showing a clear gradient pattern. Compared with adolescents without food insecurity, those experiencing food insecurity were less likely to meet one (RRR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.74-0.93), two (RRR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.58-0.83), and all three guidelines (RRR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.29-0.76). In analyses of behavioral combinations, food insecurity was consistently associated with a lower likelihood of engaging in favorable movement patterns. Stronger associations were observed for combinations involving sleep, including sleep only (RRR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.57-0.87), MVPA + sleep (RRR = 0.56, 95% CI: 0.41-0.75), and screen time + sleep (RRR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.52-0.92), whereas no significant association was found for MVPA alone. Food insecurity is associated with lower adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines and less favorable combinations of movement behaviors among adolescents. These findings highlight the importance of addressing social determinants alongside integrated behavior patterns to promote adolescent health.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary rescue and evidence-based nursing intervention for severe postoperative hypoxemia in a former preterm infant: a case report.
papers.abstract: To summarize the multidisciplinary rescue and evidence-based nursing experience for a former 32-week preterm infant with severe hypoxemia (SpO₂ min 29%) after inguinal hernia surgery, and to describe the key elements of postoperative airway crisis management with reference to international guidelines and domestic cases. Clinical data of the infant admitted on June 18, 2025, were retrospectively analyzed. The infant developed progressive SpO₂ decline to 29% with apnea post-extubation. A multidisciplinary team performed airway crisis management, stepwise oxygen therapy, glucocorticoid therapy, and family empowerment. A structured "warning-intervention-evaluation" closed-loop management model was implemented, and HHFNC application was initiated within 30 min post-extubation. Following extubation, the infant developed desaturation to 75-78%, which recovered to 99% with mask ventilation. During a subsequent failed reintubation attempt, SpO₂ dropped again to 29% and recovered again after mask ventilation. Spontaneous breathing resumed within 30 min. After transfer to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), stridor resolved, and no hypoxemic recurrence occurred. Seizures were controlled, with normal CT/EEG. Discharge occurred on day 8, with no events at 1-week follow-up. Key observations in this case included: ①multidisciplinary team response time was < 1 min in this case; ② the combination of corticosteroids, nebulization, and HHFNC was temporally associated with the avoidance of reintubation in this case; ③ implementation of a structured seizure monitoring protocol was associated with recognition of neurological symptoms within 10 min of onset. Rapid multidisciplinary response, evidence-based stratified interventions, and comprehensive perioperative management may be important for severe postoperative hypoxemia in former preterm infants. The closed-loop management model and early HHFNC strategy provide a reference pathway for perioperative care, but their effectiveness requires further validation in larger studies. However, the absence of long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up limits conclusions regarding neurological recovery.

papers.title: Digital phenotyping for monitoring mental health outcomes in patients with cancer: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Patients with cancer often experience anxiety, depression, psychological distress, and fear throughout diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation. Conventional mental health assessment relies mainly on periodic clinical evaluations and patient-reported measures, which may increase patient burden and inadequately capture dynamic psychological changes in daily life. Digital phenotyping enables the passive and continuous collection of behavioral and physiological data through smartphones, wearable devices, and other sensors; however, evidence for its application to mental health in patients with cancer remains limited and fragmented. PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception to July 2026 using terms related to digital phenotyping and cancer. A supplementary targeted sensitivity search was also conducted. Two reviewers independently screened the records and extracted data on study characteristics, participant characteristics, data collection characteristics, mental health outcomes, assessment tools, and associations found. A total of 17 studies involving 829 participants were included. Wearable devices and smartphones were used for passive data collection, most commonly incorporating accelerometers and GPS. Derived features covered activity, location and mobility, sleep, cardiac physiology, and device-use behavior. Depression and anxiety were the most frequently assessed mental health outcomes. Higher physical activity was generally associated with lower depression, anxiety, sadness, and psychological distress, whereas greater sedentary behavior and disrupted sleep or rest-activity rhythms were associated with higher psychological symptom levels. Digital phenotyping shows potential to support remote mental health monitoring in patients with cancer. However, the current evidence remains limited and heterogeneous and is insufficient to support the routine clinical implementation of digital phenotyping. Future research should prioritize larger-scale, standardized, multicenter prospective studies.

papers.title: Sleep disturbances in children with cystic fibrosis on highly effective modulator therapy referred for polysomnography.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are increasingly recognized in children with cystic fibrosis (CF), including those on highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT), but polysomnographic data remain limited and the factors associated with these disturbances are poorly understood. Single-center retrospective review of polysomnographic data from 2015 to 2025 in children with CF to evaluate associations between sleep outcomes and non-pulmonary comorbidities known to affect sleep including iron deficiency, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety/depression. Sixty children with CF underwent polysomnography (mean age 8.8 ± 4.6 years) with 58% receiving HEMTs for an average of 2.1 ± 1.4 years. Sleep complaints were common overall: snoring (85%), insomnia symptoms (71%), restless sleep (71%), hypersomnolence (29%). Although snoring was more prevalent in the non-HEMT group (p = 0.008), children on HEMTs had 4.7-fold higher odds of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), independent of age, nutritional status, adenoid/tonsillar hypertrophy, and dependence on nocturnal feeds (p = 0.037). They also had poorer sleep efficiency (p = 0.028) and more prolonged sleep-onset latency (p = 0.038) as compared to children not on modulators, even after accounting for age differences between the groups. Adenoid/tonsillar hypertrophy and nocturnal feeding both emerged as being significant predictors of OSA, independent of age, nutritional status, and HEMT use (p < 0.05). Iron deficiency, present in 70% regardless of HEMT use, was associated with restless sleep (p = 0.0002) and insomnia symptoms (p = 0.037). ADHD and anxiety/depression, each present in approximately 22% independent of HEMT, were also associated with multiple subjective and objective markers of disturbed sleep. Iron deficiency, neurodevelopmental/mental health comorbidities appear to be common among children with CF undergoing polysomnography and were associated with both subjective sleep complaints and objective polysomnographic abnormalities. Children receiving HEMTs had greater odds of OSA and differences in sleep architecture compared with those not receiving modulators. Nocturnal feedings also appear to adversely influence sleep in children with CF, independent of HEMT use. These findings highlight the importance of considering non-pulmonary comorbidities when evaluating sleep disturbances in pediatric CF and support the need for prospective longitudinal studies to better characterize these associations.

papers.title: Peripheral sensory clocks drive nitroglycerin-induced rhythmic pain sensitivity.
papers.abstract: Mounting evidence has revealed circadian rhythms in pain sensitivity across multiple pain conditions, but the mechanisms that generate these rhythmic pain sensitivities remain unclear. We combined genetic models with tissue-specific knockout of the essential clock gene Bmal1 and a well-established nitroglycerin (NTG)-induced headache mouse model. Von Frey assays were performed to measure mechanical hypersensitivity at different times of the day. Circadian activity behavior, sleep and clock gene expression were also measured. Using trigeminal ganglion (TG) and dorsal root ganglion (DRG) sensory neuron-specific Bmal1 knockout mice, we show that, in both male and female mice, loss of Bmal1 completely abolishes the diurnal rhythm of pain sensitivity but does not perturb basal nociception of NTG-induced hypersensitivity. In contrast, suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN)-specific Bmal1 deletion in male mice eliminates circadian locomotor rhythms without altering rhythmic pain sensitivity, demonstrating that the central pacemaker SCN is not required for circadian rhythms of pain sensitivity. Dual deletion of Bmal1 in both SCN and sensory neurons replicates the sensory neuron-specific phenotype, confirming the dominant role of the peripheral sensory neuron clocks in male mice. Although sensory neuron Bmal1 loss alters sleep architecture, the free-running circadian period length remains intact. Together, these findings reveal that local molecular clocks in the peripheral nervous system drive diurnal rhythmicity of NTG-induced pain independently of the SCN.
papers.journal: The journal of headache and pain

papers.title: Development and internal evaluation of a nomogram for identifying current sleep disturbance in patients with colorectal cancer undergoing chemotherapy: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify factors associated with current sleep disturbance (SD) in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) undergoing chemotherapy and to develop and internally evaluate a nomogram for estimating the probability of current SD. A total of 630 patients with CRC undergoing chemotherapy were recruited from five hospitals in China. Participants were assessed using the Demographic Information Questionnaire, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), while clinical assessment data and laboratory test results at admission were obtained from electronic medical records. The data were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a 7:3 ratio. Univariable analyses and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with SD in patients with CRC undergoing chemotherapy. The training set was used for multivariable logistic regression modeling and nomogram development, whereas the validation set was used to evaluate the discrimination and calibration of the fixed model. In addition, 500 bootstrap resamples were performed within the training set for internal validation. The overall prevalence of current SD was 68.7%. Gender, disease duration, ECOG performance status, HADS-D score, serum potassium, and albumin were independently associated with current SD and were included in the final nomogram. The model showed an AUC of 0.762 (95% CI, 0.716~0.808) in the training set and 0.712 (95% CI, 0.635~0.789) in the validation set. Bootstrap internal validation in the training set yielded a mean absolute calibration error of 0.022. In the validation set, the mean absolute calibration error (Eavg) was 0.055, with a calibration intercept of 0.318, a calibration slope of 0.667, and a Brier score of 0.188. Patients with CRC undergoing chemotherapy had a high burden of current SD. The nomogram may assist in identifying patients with a higher probability of current SD who may warrant further sleep assessment.

papers.title: Multidimensional frailty trajectories and associated factors in older adults with pulmonary tuberculosis: a prospective longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Older adults with pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) are particularly vulnerable to multidimensional frailty. However, longitudinal evidence regarding patterns of frailty changes after antituberculosis treatment initiation and their associated factors remains limited. This study aimed to identify distinct trajectories of multidimensional frailty among older adults with pulmonary TB and to examine the associations of anxiety, depression, insomnia, and clinical characteristics with different frailty trajectories. A prospective longitudinal study was conducted among 251 older adults with pulmonary TB. Multidimensional frailty was assessed using the Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI) at 1, 3, 9, and 12 months after initiation of antituberculosis treatment. At baseline, anxiety and depression were assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and insomnia was assessed using the Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). Latent class growth analysis was used to identify distinct trajectories of multidimensional frailty. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was subsequently applied to select candidate variables, followed by multinomial logistic regression to examine factors associated with trajectory membership. Three distinct trajectories of multidimensional frailty were identified: high-frailty decreasing (13.1%), moderate-frailty improving (17.9%), and low-frailty persistent (68.9%) trajectory. Multinomial LASSO regression selected 14 candidate variables potentially associated with frailty trajectory membership. Compared with the low-frailty persistence trajectory, a history of smoking (OR = 4.668, 95% CI 1.217-7.904, P = 0.025) was associated with greater odds of membership in the high-frailty decreasing trajectory. In contrast, higher albumin levels (OR = 0.892, 95% CI 0.798-0.996, P = 0.043), absence of anxiety symptoms (OR = 0.093, P = 0.001), absence of depressive symptoms (OR = 0.044, P < 0.001), and absence of insomnia (OR = 0.020, P < 0.001) were associated with lower odds of membership in the high-frailty decreasing trajectory. Compared with the low-frailty persistence trajectory, absence of anxiety symptoms, absence of insomnia, and absence of depressive symptoms were also associated with lower odds of membership in the moderate-frailty improvement trajectory. Multidimensional frailty exhibited substantial heterogeneity among older adults with pulmonary TB during antituberculosis treatment. Baseline anxiety, depressive symptoms, and insomnia, together with albumin level, were associated with distinct frailty trajectories. Early frailty screening during antituberculosis treatment, integrated with assessment of psychological and sleep status and routine laboratory indicators, may facilitate trajectory-based risk stratification and individualized management of frailty in older adults with pulmonary TB. Not applicable.

papers.title: Effect of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to ropivacaine in stellate ganglion block on postoperative sleep quality in patients undergoing thyroid cancer surgery: a randomized double-blind controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Postoperative sleep disturbance is common after thyroid cancer surgery and may delay recovery. Stellate ganglion block (SGB) can regulate sympathetic activity, but single local anesthetic blockade has limited duration. This trial aimed to evaluate whether perineural addition of dexmedetomidine to ropivacaine in right-sided SGB could improve early postoperative sleep quality among thyroid cancer patients. This randomized, double-blind controlled trial included 60 patients in the per-protocol efficacy analysis (n = 30 per group); safety and recovery outcomes were assessed in all 62 treated participants. Before anesthesia induction, patients received ultrasound-guided right-sided SGB with a 6-mL injectate: 0.2% ropivacaine alone in group R and 0.2% ropivacaine plus dexmedetomidine 0.5 µg/kg in group RD. Actigraphy assessed sleep on the preoperative night, surgery night (D0), and postoperative nights 1 (D1) and 2 (D2). The retrospectively specified primary endpoint was D1 sleep efficiency (SE). Secondary outcomes included other sleep measures, the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), resting pain, and rescue analgesia; hemodynamic outcomes were exploratory. On D1, SE was higher in group RD than in group R (88.3 ± 5.8% vs. 81.3 ± 6.7%). The adjusted mean difference was 7.1 percentage points (95% CI 3.8 to 10.3; P < 0.001). In a post hoc Holm-adjusted analysis of the six originally registered sleep outcomes, group × time interactions remained statistically significant for SE, total sleep time (TST), wake after sleep onset (WASO), sleep onset latency (SOL), and ISI, but not for number of awakenings (NA). On D1, group RD also had longer TST (+ 59.4 min; P < 0.01), shorter WASO (- 24.3 min; P < 0.01), and shorter SOL (- 6.5 min; P < 0.001). Among the secondary outcomes, early ISI and HADS score differences favored group RD but were exploratory because standard recall periods overlapped across assessments; their clinical meaning is uncertain. Other secondary findings included lower overall resting pain scores and less rescue analgesic use in group RD. No serious adverse events occurred. The dexmedetomidine-ropivacaine regimen for right-sided SGB was associated with better early postoperative actigraphy-derived sleep outcomes than ropivacaine alone in patients undergoing thyroid cancer surgery. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600118983. Registered 13 February 2026, retrospectively registered.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing, Insomnia and Their Comorbidity: Associations With Masseter Mechanical Pain Sensitivity in Adults With Painful Temporomandibular Disorder.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in temporomandibular disorder (TMD), but associations of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), insomnia and their co-occurrence (COMISA) to mechanical pain sensitivity remain uncertain. To test differences in masseter pressure pain threshold (PPT) across sleep phenotypes in adults with painful TMD, and to quantify independent associations of continuous sleep indices with PPT. We studied 172 adults with painful TMD. SDB was defined by overnight oximetry (3% oxygen desaturation index [ODI3%] ≥ 5 events/h) and insomnia by the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) ≥ 15. (TMD reference group, n = 65; TMD + SDB, n = 41; TMD + insomnia, n = 41; TMD + COMISA, n = 25). PPTs were measured by algometry. Continuous sleep indices were Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), ISI, ODI3% and sleep time with oxygen saturation < 90% (T90%). Group comparisons used Kruskal-Wallis and ART-ANCOVA; hierarchical regression evaluated associations. PPT did not differ significantly across sleep phenotypes (H = 3.06, p = 0.38; ART-ANCOVA, p = 0.63). In the fully adjusted model, higher PSQI (B = -12.56 kPa, HC3 95% CI -24.50 to -0.61; p = 0.040) and ESS (B = -11.47 kPa, HC3 95% CI -21.78 to -1.17; p = 0.029) were associated with lower PPT. After excluding isolated arthralgia, the PSQI association persisted, whereas the ESS remained negative but non-significant. Mechanical pain sensitivity did not differ across categorical sleep phenotypes. Poorer sleep quality and daytime sleepiness were independently associated with lower PPTs, but these cross-sectional findings do not establish causality or the superiority of continuous measures.

papers.title: A Photoelectrically Activated Neural Stem Cell Matrix for Nerve Repair.
papers.abstract: Stem cell therapy for nerve injury requires a local environment that supports cell delivery and regulates neurotrophic output. An injectable PN-junction-based biomimetic neural matrix (PNBM) integrates silicon PN-junction microfragments and neural stem cells within a thermoresponsive hyaluronic acid-methylcellulose-laminin hydrogel. Under 635 nm illumination, the microfragments generate reproducible photovoltages and amplify intracellular calcium responses. Compared with light alone, PN-junction photoactivation reduces first-spike latency by 91% and increases firing frequency 3.45-fold. Transcriptomic analysis identifies phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) pathway enrichment, while protein assays demonstrate increased secretion of nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, and glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor. In noncontact cocultures, photoactivated PNBM increases process extension and burst frequency in HT22 hippocampal cells and promotes Schwann cell alignment and myelin basic protein expression. In rats with optic nerve crush, treatment preserves retinal structure, reduces the astroglial lesion response, and improves visual evoked potentials. In sciatic nerve crush, it improves locomotor performance, motor electrophysiology, axon-myelin organization, and gastrocnemius preservation. PNBM couples semiconductor photoactivation to enhanced stem cell trophic output and provides a locally delivered bioelectronic matrix for central and peripheral nerve repair.

papers.title: Adherence to the MIND diet and psychoneurological symptoms, inflammation, and brain volumes in postmenopausal breast cancer survivors: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Examine the association between adherence to the MIND diet and psychoneurological symptoms, inflammatory markers, and brain volumes of postmenopausal breast cancer (BC) survivors. This cross-sectional study included an analytical sample of 21 BC survivors, 3-12 months postchemotherapy. Dietary data were collected via electronic food frequency questionnaire. Psychoneurological symptoms (cognitive impairment, fatigue, sleep disturbance, depression, and anxiety) were self-reported using validated questionnaires. Serum inflammatory biomarkers were measured using ELISA. Magnetic resonance imaging assessed brain volumes. Multivariate regressions assessed associations of log-MIND diet adherence with symptom burden (primary), individual symptoms, inflammation, and brain volumes (secondary), and binary MIND recommendations with symptoms, inflammation, and brain volumes (exploratory). Analyses were adjusted for false discovery rate using Benjamini-Hochberg method (p_adj < 0.05). Lower symptom burden was associated with higher berry intake (OR = 0.123, p = 0.001, p_adj = 0.015). While lower depression scores were associated with higher other vegetable intake (β = - 0.868, p = 0.001, p_adj = 0.017). Several nominally significant (p < 0.05, p_adj ≥ 0.05) results were observed between lower symptom burden and adherence to the MIND diet, greater intakes of green leafy vegetables, other vegetables, and beans and legumes. Lower anxiety, depression, fatigue, and sleep disturbance scores were nominally associated with higher intakes of berries, cheese, and other vegetables. Lower inflammatory marker concentrations were nominally associated with higher intake of berries and other vegetables as well as lower intake of butter and margarine. Larger subcortical gray matter volumes were nominally associated with consuming berries within the recommended amount (≥ 5 servings/week). Adherence to the MIND diet, specifically higher berry intake, was associated with lower psychoneurological symptom burden among postmenopausal BC survivors. Recommended intake of MIND diet components was also associated with individual symptoms, inflammation, and brain volumes. Further research is needed to confirm these findings.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

papers.title: Consciousness, complexity, and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: Consciousness remains one of science's most challenging problems because it cannot be exhaustively characterized as a single function, computation, or behavior; it also refers to the presence and organization of subjective experience. This position paper integrates clinical neurology, neurophysiology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis, embodied cognition, moral neuroscience, theoretical physics, philosophy of mind, and neurotechnology. We argue that, despite major advances in identifying neural correlates, computational models, and behavioral markers, contemporary consciousness research has not resolved the explanatory gap between objective description and subjective experience. We propose that claims about consciousness at neurophysiological, embodied, cognitive, social, and ontological levels should be coordinated through explicit cross-level constraints rather than merged into a single unitary theory. These domains have different evidential roles and are not all constituents of consciousness. Perturbational measures of cortical complexity, including the Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) and its state-transition variant (PCIst), support assessment of preserved conscious capacity in studied human populations. They do not independently determine a clinical diagnosis or phenomenal content. Evidence from aphasia, sleep, anesthesia, and disorders of consciousness also demonstrates dissociations among language, wakefulness, behavioral responsiveness, and conscious experience. Perspectives from embodied simulation, mind-object identity, quantum information, and the philosophy of physics are treated here as heuristic stress tests rather than as mechanistic accounts; they keep open foundational questions concerning subjectivity, representation, and the role of the observer. We advocate constrained pluralism, a methodological framework in which consciousness is conceptualized as an integrated, embodied, relational, and temporally extended process. Such an approach provides a coherent foundation for future research while strengthening the dialogue between neuroscience, clinical practice, philosophy, and neuroethics.

papers.title: Association between sleep health and ocular diseases: a population-based study.
papers.abstract: The association between sleep health and ocular diseases among U.S. adults remains insufficiently understood. Using publicly available data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005-8, weighted restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and subgroup analyses were performed to examine the associations of sleep health with the prevalence of ocular diseases, including glaucoma, cataract, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy. A total of 5549 individuals were included, among whom 328 (5.91%) had glaucoma, 685 (12.34%) had cataract, 430 (7.75%) had AMD, and 1031 (18.60%) had diabetic retinopathy. A U-shaped relationship was observed between sleep duration and ocular diseases (glaucoma, cataracts, AMD, diabetic retinopathy) (all P for nonlinearity <0.05). It is evident that ocular disease risk decreases with increasing sleep duration, reaching the lowest risk around 7.0-8.0 h. Additionally, poor sleep patterns (abnormal sleep duration, trouble sleeping, sleep disorders) were risk factors for ocular disease. In summary, the study observed a U-shaped association of sleep duration with the risk of glaucoma, cataract, AMD, and diabetic retinopathy. Both short and long sleep durations or poor sleep patterns increased the prevalence of ocular disease.

papers.title: Mapping global glymphatic system research (2012-2025): a scientometric and knowledge-mapping review integrating bioinformatics perspectives on aging.
papers.abstract: The glymphatic system is a newly discovered brain-wide clearance pathway offering promising novel therapeutic interventions across diverse medical conditions. Accordingly, a comprehensive overview mapping scientific knowledge is currently urgent. Our study examined the spatiotemporal evolution of research output, institutions, authors, journals, as well as their mutual interactions. With publications steadily increasing, the field has shifted from animal studies toward human research, and demonstrated an evolutionary trajectory from fundamental mechanisms to advancing clinical applications. Keywords analysis identified five thematic clusters covering disease associations, system dynamics and drug delivery, sleep and aging-related clearance, neuroimaging, and cognitive impairment including Alzheimer's disease. Analysis of GEO datasets identified aging and glymphatic related genes converging on PI3K-Akt and FoxO signaling, central regulators of survival, stress responses, and longevity. Our findings highlight the need for approaches capable of quantifying perivascular fluid transport and glial-vascular interactions, especially in the context of aging-related structural change. Such cross-disciplinary convergence is essential for translating mechanistic insights into clinically actionable, glymphatic-targeted interventions that may have promising potential for various brain disorders.

papers.title: A steady-state visual evoked potential-based brain-computer interface dataset in children and adolescents.
papers.abstract: The development of steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for children has been limited, in part, by the scarcity of publicly available pediatric SSVEP datasets. In addition, an established issue with SSVEP-based BCI systems is the visual fatigue and discomfort caused by high contrast flashing visual stimuli. Here, we present an open-access pediatric SSVEP dataset (n = 47; age 5-18 years), comprised of EEG recorded during a standard laboratory-style SSVEP experiment, and a user-choice led online 4-target SSVEP-based game. The standard experiment evaluated 12 SSVEP stimuli varying in contrast and size, weighing comfort ratings with SSVEP signal strength to determine an individualized SSVEP stimulus for each participant. Participants subsequently completed the online SSVEP-based BCI game using both their personalized stimulus and a standard high-contrast stimulus. The signal quality of the dataset was validated through comparisons with two existing SSVEP datasets, demonstrating similar spectral peaks and signal-to-noise ratios at fundamental and harmonic frequencies. This dataset provides EEG data from children aged 5-18 (mean 12.6 ± 3.9) years to support pediatric-specific SSVEP stimulus optimization as well as signal processing advancements in SSVEP-based BCI research.

papers.title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior.
papers.abstract: The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio - a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment - as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

papers.title: Ergonomic evaluation of an age-friendly foot dorsiflexion stretching device for adults aged 55 years or older.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSupported stretching devices may facilitate accessible lower-limb movement, but candidate settings should be evaluated without equating physiological responses with functional benefit.ObjectiveTo examine physiological and perceptual responses to a foot dorsiflexion stretching prototype and identify candidate settings for further evaluation.MethodsThe within-subject evaluation involved 20 adults aged 55 years or older. Prototype footplate inclinations of 22°, 24° and 26° preceded 30-70-s duration conditions at 22° in a fixed sequence. Walking surface electromyography (sEMG) following exposure was evaluated separately for four right-leg muscles and for dynamic and static modes. Frontal electroencephalography (EEG) followed walking. Available tabulated summaries were analysed using participant-level baseline differences, sample standard deviations and nominal 95% confidence intervals. Eight semantic descriptors were reported individually.ResultsAt 22°, mean tabulated walking-amplitude changes were positive for all four muscles in both modes; at 26°, they were negative. Comfortable-item means were 4.55 in both modes at 22° and 4.60/4.50 at 60 s. Several, but not all, profiles were largest around 50-60 s. Matching physiological entries at 22° and 60 s did not provide independent validation. Record inconsistencies and incomplete measurement documentation limited interpretation.ConclusionsA 22° prototype footplate inclination and 60-s exposure are candidate settings only for this prototype, sample and sequence. The findings do not establish an optimum, mode-specific functional benefits, clinical efficacy or safety thresholds.

papers.title: Lactobacillus Fermentation-Derived γ-Aminobutyric Acid Improves Sleep Parameters in Invertebrate and Vertebrate Models.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the sleep-promoting effects of Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) produced by Lactobacillus fermentation using invertebrate and vertebral models. The activity of GABA derived from lactic acid bacteria (GABArelax®) was analyzed through subjective day-night movement and sleep-related parameters in fruit flies (Drosophila melanogaster) and sleep duration, neurotransmitter-related factors, and brain waves in ICR mice and SD-rats. In Drosophila, GABArelax® increased total sleep time and reduced nighttime and daytime locomotor activity, with the 3% treatment producing effects comparable to those of benzodiazepine. Video-tracking analysis further demonstrated that 2% and 3% GABArelax® reduced the total distance traveled, locomotor velocity, and overall mobility, while exerting relatively limited effects on the total duration of active and inactive behavior. In ICR mice, GABArelax® increased the mRNA expression of GABAergic and serotonergic receptors, including GABAA-R, GABAB-R1, GABAB-R2, and Htr1a. These transcriptional changes were accompanied by elevated brain concentrations of GABA and 5-hydroxytryptamine and enhanced expression of antioxidant defense-related genes, including SOD, Gpx1, and CAT. Electroencephalographic analysis in SD-rats showed that GABArelax® reduced wakefulness and prolonged total sleep duration. This increase was predominantly attributable to an extension of non-rapid eye movement sleep, whereas high-dose administration reduced REM sleep and enhanced δ-wave activity, an electrophysiological marker of deep sleep. Overall, these findings demonstrate that GABArelax® promotes sleep through coordinated regulation of GABAergic and serotonergic neurotransmission, reinforcement of antioxidant defense, and improvement of sleep architecture. GABArelax® therefore represents a promising food-derived functional ingredient for the management of sleep disturbances and the improvement of sleep quality.

papers.title: Sleep and mental health outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy: A matched cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to compare sleep quality, mental health symptoms, and PASC outcomes among pregnant and non-pregnant participants with and without prior COVID-19 infection. A matched cross-sectional study design was undertaken, comparing four groups: 1) Not Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; 2) Not Pregnant, prior COVID-19; 3) Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; and 4) Pregnant and prior COVID-19. A total of 1,868 women were included in the analysis (934 pregnant and 934 not pregnant). Among participants with prior COVID-19, those who were pregnant had significantly more comorbidities, and higher hospitalization rates, compared to those not pregnant with prior COVID-19. Overall, prior COVID-19 infection was consistently associated with poorer sleep quality and more sleep disturbances, regardless of pregnancy status. In addition, participants who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 were more likely to report a shorter sleep duration of <5 and <6 hours per night, compared with those not pregnant with no prior COVID-19. Adjusted analyses showed pregnant participants with prior COVID-19 had worse sleep quality and more frequent sleep problems than non-pregnant participants without prior COVID-19. Furthermore, those who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 had a 1.76 to 2.69 times increased odds of developing PASC symptoms, compared to those not pregnant. These high rates of persistent PASC symptoms reported at 3 and 6 months, indicating more prolonged or delayed symptom expression. They also experienced worse mental health outcomes, with the prevalence ratio of having depression and anxiety symptoms occurring 1.89 and 1.72 times higher, respectively, among pregnant individuals with a history of COVID-19. Prior COVID-19 infection should be considered when assessing sleep and mental health in pregnancy due to its association with long-term PASC symptoms. Tailored post-COVID care, maternal health policies, and vaccination should be prioritized.

papers.title: Short sleep for whom? Toward a personalized definition of sleep duration adequacy.
Functional Neuroimaging in Tinnitus: Review of Recent Advances.
papers.abstract: Chronic subjective tinnitus, the perception of sound without an external source, is highly prevalent, clinically heterogeneous, and lacks a cure and objective diagnostic tests. This review examines how functional neuroimaging is closing that gap. Hemodynamic (functional MRI [fMRI], functional near-infrared spectroscopy, PET) and electrophysiological (electroencephalography, magnetoencephalography) modalities redefine tinnitus as a brain-network disorder involving auditory, limbic, and cognitive systems. Altered default mode network connectivity, auditory-limbic hyperconnectivity, and reduced thalamocortical inhibition are emerging as candidate biomarkers that track severity and may help stratify patients. These findings increasingly guide therapies such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and real-time fMRI neurofeedback.

papers.title: Tinnitus and Psychiatry.
papers.abstract: Tinnitus disorder, defined by clinically significant psychological distress accompanying the auditory percept, is associated with substantial functional impairment yet remains absent from current diagnostic classification systems. Psychiatric comorbidities such as insomnia, depression, and anxiety, are common and appear to interact bidirectionally with tinnitus distress. Treatment of these psychiatric comorbidities should be an essential part of the management of patients with tinnitus disorder. Recognition of tinnitus disorder as a formal diagnostic entity could improve access to evidence-based psychiatric care through existing mental health services while complementing the interdisciplinary management essential for optimal treatment.

papers.title: Cancer-related cognitive impairment: Mechanisms and clinical implications.
papers.abstract: Due to diagnosis and therapeutic progress, cancer patients' survival is improving, and the long-term consequences of oncological treatments have become a growing clinical priority. Among these, Cancer-Related Cognitive Impairment (CRCI) represents one of the most frequently reported sequelae, affecting various cognitive domains in a substantial proportion of survivors across cancer types and treatment modalities. Once attributed to chemotherapy alone, CRCI is now understood as a broader phenomenon arising across multiple treatment modalities, reflecting a more complex and multifactorial clinical reality. Beginning with a critical appraisal of the methodological challenges, this review successively addresses prevalence and temporal evolution of the CRCI, the neurobiological mechanisms underlying cognitive difficulties including direct treatment-induced neurotoxicity and sustained neuroinflammatory cascades, the genetic vulnerabilities modulating individual susceptibility, the constellation of person-related variables encompassing psychological distress, sleep disturbances, social factors, age, and level of education. In addition, CRCI is a heterogeneous condition, most often transient yet occasionally persistent, shaped by the interplay of biological and psychosocial factors. However, limitations remain. Methodological inconsistencies limit strong CRCI characterization, many neurobiological pathways, as well as their interactions, remain partially elucidated, and the predominance of breast cancer patients in the evaluated populations precludes firm conclusions to other cancer types. Future research should integrate the multidimensional nature of CRCI, prioritize longitudinal designs and multidisciplinary approaches, broader cancer population representation, and the development of more ecologically valid assessment tools to address the unmet needs of survivors affected by cognitive impairment.
