papers.title: Large-Scale Neural Slowing Measured with Electroencephalography Indexes Secondary Thalamic Degeneration in Stroke.
papers.abstract: A central priority in stroke recovery research is the development of useful biomarkers that reveal underlying disease states to aid diagnosis, prognosis, stratification, and treatment, ideally using tools that are readily available in clinical settings. Large-scale neural slowing has the potential to be such a biomarker, but its usefulness is currently limited by uncertainty about its nature and relation to underlying pathophysiology. In this work, we sought to address these gaps by parameterizing abnormal resting-state electroencephalography spectral features across the scalp and investigating their relationship to thalamic atrophy and dysfunction, using structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and a computational model of corticothalamic circuit dynamics, respectively. As predicted, stroke patients (n = 25; 15 males, 10 females) exhibited widespread spectral abnormalities, including significantly increased aperiodic exponent and offset, lower alpha frequency, and reduced beta power, which together can account for the frequently observed shift in power toward low frequencies after stroke. Furthermore, corticothalamic models fit to power spectral densities across the scalp inferred broad thalamic disinhibition. Crucially, these abnormalities (except beta reductions) were strongly associated with ipsilesional thalamic atrophy measured with MRI, despite the lack of direct thalamus damage in this sample. Overall, this work provides a deeper characterization of large-scale electrophysiological abnormalities after stroke and reinforces their potential as clinically feasible biomarkers of poststroke pathophysiology.

papers.title: Effect of esketamine on postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing spine surgery: a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
Genetic basis of latitudinal adaptation in Chinook salmon.
papers.abstract: Organisms can experience very different selective pressures across their latitudinal range, yet the genetic changes that underlie phenotypic differences across latitudes are poorly understood. Pacific salmon are renowned for extreme life-history variation and local adaptation to specific environments. We sequenced 137 whole genomes of Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) sampled along the Pacific Coast of North America to predict genetic adaptation across latitudes. We tested latitudinal gradients in five genes previously linked to polymorphisms in two types of phenotypic traits that vary with latitude in salmonids: timing of migration and rate of maturation: CLOCK1A, CLOCK1B, VGLL3, SIX6 and ROCK1/GREB1L. Allelic variation in all five candidate genes was indeed strongly associated with latitude. Many of the same single nucleotide polymorphisms in ROCK1/GREB1L were previously linked to a polymorphism in the timing of adult migration in the south of the range. Additionally, we found strong correlations with latitude in other genes that interact with the gene pathways previously linked to migration or maturation (including the circadian clock and Hippo signalling pathways) and in multiple organs (especially the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis), suggesting that changes preferentially affect functional clusters of interacting genes. This has implications for the conservation of organisms across latitudinal clines and their adaptation to future climates.

papers.title: Oscillatory power and functional network coordination during graded semantic Go/NoGo processing in amnestic mild cognitive impairment.
papers.abstract: Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) may involve altered associative-executive coordination during semantic Go/NoGo processing, but the underlying oscillatory and network-level EEG differences remain incompletely characterized. To characterize oscillatory activity and functional network coordination in aMCI across Go/NoGo tasks differing in semantic demand. EEG was recorded from 31 patients with aMCI and 30 healthy controls during three Go/NoGo paradigms. Delta/theta power and weighted phase-lag index (wPLI)-based networks were examined in predefined N2 (130-210 ms) and P3 (300-400 ms) windows, with complementary alpha/beta analyses. Exploratory frontal-theta (4-8 Hz)/central-beta (13-30 Hz) phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) and amplitude-amplitude coupling (AAC) were assessed over 0-1000 ms. aMCI participants showed lower accuracy in Go/NoGo1 and Go/NoGo2 and longer reaction time in Go/NoGo2. The clearest power difference was lower frontal NoGo theta during the Go/NoGo3 P3 window (2.00 ± 0.28 vs. 3.23 ± 0.39 dB; p = 0.014). During Go/NoGo1 P3-window NoGo trials, aMCI showed nominally lower theta-network global efficiency and clustering and longer characteristic path length (p = 0.008-0.010); Group × Task interactions were not significant. Exploratory Go/NoGo2 NoGo PAC and AAC were higher in aMCI in the total signal (p = 0.039 and 0.029), as was the AAC NoGo-Go contrast (p = 0.036). These effects were not significant after subtraction of the condition-averaged ERP. The findings indicate heterogeneous task-dependent electrophysiological differences consistent with altered associative-executive coordination in aMCI. Cross-frequency effects were preliminary and sensitive to ERP subtraction.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology

papers.title: Interpretable MEG decoding of perceived speech: Source-space patterns and the stimulus features that drive retrieval.
papers.abstract: Short segments of perceived speech can be retrieved from non-invasive magnetoencephalographic (MEG) recordings by a deep network trained with a CLIP-style objective against wav2vec 2.0 audio embeddings (Défossez et al., 2023; Baevski et al., 2020; Radford et al., 2021). Such studies do not convert their weights into the notions used in classical electrophysiology. Although the spatial filters in the front end of Défossez et al. (2023) could in principle be mapped to source topographies, the dynamic properties of those sources remain out of reach. Which properties of the speech stream contribute to the decoding is equally unclear. Here we scrutinize a decoder with a physiologically motivated, factorized spatial-temporal front end that permits joint interpretation of learned spatial topographies and temporal patterns in relation to the MEG forward model. Building on the framework of Petrosyan et al. (2021, 2022), we replace the 2D Fourier spatial attention of Défossez et al. (2023) with a layer parameterized by spherical harmonics (Sivakumar et al., 2016), reduce the subject-specific representation from 270 to K=25 branches, and add trainable temporal filters so that each branch has an explicit learned spatial filter and temporal response. Ocular and cardiac components are removed before training, since either could supply stimulus-locked information that would otherwise be mistaken for cortical. On the cleaned MEG-MASC dataset (Gwilliams et al., 2023) the model reaches 39.75±0.34% Top-1 accuracy among 1005 candidates across six model initializations (mean ± SD), with approximately 20× fewer trainable parameters in the decoder. Its learned spatial patterns can be mapped through a cortical inverse model (Petrosyan et al., 2021; Haufe et al., 2014), yielding approximate source-magnitude projections with recurrent bilateral structure over lateral cortex, concentrated around temporal and adjacent peri-Sylvian regions. Paired MEG occlusion, replacing feature-marked speech segments with matched donors from feature-present and feature-absent intervals, shows significant positive effects for 15 of 19 tested stimulus features, the largest effects being silence, sound intensity, vowels and acoustic onsets. Intriguingly, the randomly ordered word lists behave oppositely: replacing word-list MEG with MEG recorded during coherent narrative improves retrieval relative to word-list donor MEG. The wav2vec target can be reduced to about twelve learned feature dimensions with only a small reduction in retrieval accuracy, whereas strong temporal compression causes a clear performance loss. Decoders with physiologically interpretable spatial-temporal front ends can thus serve as knowledge-discovery tools: their learned weights can be converted into source-space and temporal patterns, while input interventions reveal what the decision rule relies on.

papers.title: Noise burden and environmental health inequalities in a growing city: a household-level health impact assessment.
papers.abstract: Road traffic noise is a major environmental health challenge and requires targeted policy interventions as urban populations and mobility demands increase. Health Impact Assessments (HIAs) can support evidence-based policymaking by quantifying health impacts, yet few HIAs have assessed road traffic noise at the household level. Collaborating with municipal stakeholders, we evaluated health impacts and equity implications of road traffic noise policies in Utrecht, the Netherlands. We applied a comparative risk assessment framework to spatially resolved road traffic noise and demographic data for existing and planned housing. Exposure-response functions (ERFs) from meta-analyses were used to estimate mortality, morbidity, annoyance, and sleep disturbance impacts from road traffic noise, with age- and sex-specific ERFs applied for mortality. Baseline exposure was compared with counterfactual levels based on the WHO guideline (53 dB Lden) and municipal targets of 63, 68, and 70 dB. Analyses were stratified by sex, age, and social versus non-social housing. Almost 40% of Utrecht's households were exposed to more than 53 dB. Meeting the WHO guideline could prevent 20 premature deaths annually and 4,158 cases of high annoyance, compared with 1 premature death and 505 high annoyance cases prevented under municipality's 63 dB target. Newly planned houses showed lower exposure and smaller relative health burdens than existing houses. Social housing bore a disproportionately high burden among existing households. Stricter road traffic noise targets, particularly towards WHO guideline levels, could yield substantial health benefits. Household-level HIA can help to identify population groups that may benefit most from noise and spatial-planning interventions.

papers.title: Ventral striatal dopamine increases following hippocampal sharp-wave ripples.
papers.abstract: The reactivation of task-related hippocampal activity during sharp-wave ripples (SWRs), often expressed as sequential "replay," is thought to contribute to behavior through both online and offline processes. During sleep and awake rest, replay supports memory consolidation, broadly defined as the updating and stabilization of knowledge structures for later use. During active task engagement, replay may also support decision-making through episodic memory retrieval and the generation of prospective scenarios1,2,3,4 (but see van der Meer and Bendor5). While disrupting SWR events impairs memory-guided behavior6,7,8,9 and augmenting them enhances such behavior,10,11 the neurophysiological mechanisms that enable replay to contribute to behavior remain unclear. Theories of replay-based learning posit the need for replay events to be followed by an evaluative signal. Dopamine (DA) is consistently associated with such teaching signals, particularly in the ventral striatum, where it reflects reward- and other prediction-error signals.12 Although hippocampal activity can influence mesolimbic DA signaling,13,14,15 whether SWRs are coupled to ventral striatal DA release is unknown. To address this, we simultaneously recorded dorsal CA1 local field potentials to detect SWRs and measured ventral striatal DA concentration using fiber photometry of the GRABDA2m sensor16 in freely moving mice. We found a significant increase in DA following SWRs. This coupling was more prominent during offline rest than during periods of immobility during behavior and was stronger following longer and higher-power SWRs. These results reveal coupling between hippocampal SWRs and striatal dopamine, providing a potential candidate mechanism through which internally generated hippocampal activity could engage evaluative signals during offline memory processing.
authors: Matthijs A A van der Meer

papers.title: Flashing light modulates insect behavior in a species-specific manner.
papers.abstract: Light is a powerful tool to study animal behavior.1-3 In contrast to natural light, almost all artificial light exhibits flicker, but most work on insect behavioral responses to light flicker focuses on flicker perceptual detection. We tested photopreference light-choice behavior across a wide range of Drosophila species in response to rhythmically flickering light using custom FLASH (flickering light of actuatable spectral hues) instrumentation and find species-specific behavioral responses and altered time-of-day-ordered behaviors that are evoked by light frequencies far beyond perceptual flicker frequency. Mutant analysis shows that behavioral responses to FLASH rely on all known classes of phototransduction, including Cryptochrome and Rhodopsin-7 expressed directly in brain neurons and the eyes. FLASH behavioral responses are abolished following ablation of the pigment-dispersing factor (PDF)-positive lateral ventral neuron circadian light input hub and in circadian mutants. These results suggest means for designing ecologically friendly light devices for species-specific insect behavioral control.

papers.title: Repetitive levodopa treatment drives cell-type-specific striatal adaptations associated with progressive dyskinesia in parkinsonian mice.
papers.abstract: The use of levodopa to manage Parkinson's disease (PD) symptoms leads to levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID) and other motor fluctuations, which worsen with disease progression and repeated treatment. Aberrant activity of striatal D1- and D2-expressing medium spiny neurons (D1-/D2-MSNs) underlies LID, but the mechanisms driving its progression remain unclear. Using the 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) mouse model of PD/LID, we combined in vivo and ex vivo recordings to isolate the effect of repeated treatment in LID worsening and other changes in the motor response to levodopa. We found that LID worsening is linked to potentiation of levodopa-evoked responses in both D1-/D2-MSNs, independent of changes in dopamine release or MSN intrinsic excitability. Instead, strengthening of glutamatergic synapses onto D1-MSNs emerged as a key signature. Moreover, we found that changes in D2-MSN activity are associated with LID duration, which parallels a reduction in D2 receptor (D2R) sensitivity. These findings reveal striatal adaptations contributing to the worsening of levodopa-related complications.

papers.title: Solutions to Reduce Burnout Syndrome Among Perioperative Healthcare Providers in Low-Resource Settings: A Qualitative Study.
papers.abstract: Research from high-income countries indicates that perioperative care providers are at high risk for burnout, with potential downstream effects on patient safety. Adequate solutions to address burnout may be particularly important in low-income countries where the effects of burnout on staff motivation and migration are likely to be compounded by the current human resources crisis. This study aimed to explore solutions to address burnout among Rwandan perioperative care providers. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with perioperative care providers (obstetricians, surgeons, anesthetists, midwives, nurses) in hospitals across all five provinces in Rwanda. Interviews were analyzed using both inductive and deductive coding following standard procedures of thematic analysis. Interviews were completed with 61 participants from all levels of public hospitals (37% teaching, 6% referral, 52% district, and 5% unknown level). The participants identified solutions at multiple levels fitting within the multilevel model of burnout.At the individual level, many drew on internal values and self-developed coping mechanisms to manage occupational stress, emphasizing the importance of fulfilling basic needs such as sleep and nutrition, and stress-relief activities such as exercise and music. At the interpersonal level, support networks involving family, friends, religious communities, and colleagues played a significant role in sustaining resilience. At the hospital level, participants found motivation through positive patient outcomes. They underscored the impact of hospital organization on workload and recommended reducing inefficiencies.Regarding the healthcare system, concerns were raised about insufficient financial resources affecting staff salaries and access to essential medicines and equipment. Participants emphasized that increasing staffing levels would improve scheduling flexibility and reduce burnout. Finally, cultural factors such as recognition, appreciation, and respectful workplace interactions were deemed essential for morale. This study illustrates that resilience among healthcare professionals is shaped by a complex interplay of individual, interpersonal, institutional, and systemic factors. While many rely on personal values and coping strategies to manage the demands of clinical work, their resilience is often strained by unmet basic needs, geographic isolation, organizational inefficiencies, and broader systemic limitations such as inadequate staffing and financing. Cultural dynamics, including recognition, respect, and workplace relationships, further influence the capacity to cope with stress. To address burnout effectively, solutions must be adapted to the Rwandan context and implemented at all levels, ranging from promoting self-care and peer support to improving hospital management and resource allocation, and to promoting innovative and evidence-based interventions.

papers.title: Flavor quality changes in fermented shrimp paste under different sterilization strategies: An integrated flavoromics and neural perception approach.
papers.abstract: Fermented shrimp paste is valued for its intense umami and distinctive aroma, yet microbial contamination limits its industrialization because conventional sterilization often degrades flavor. Here we integrate flavoromics with electroencephalography (EEG)-based neural perception to compare how pasteurization, retort sterilization, ultrasound-assisted infrared sterilization (UIR), and ultra-high-pressure instantaneous sterilization (UPI) reshape the flavor quality of traditionally fermented shrimp paste. Retort sterilization severely degrades umami amino acids and 5'-IMP while accumulating bitter amino acids, whereas UPI preserves the glutamate-IMP synergy, yielding umami intensity exceeding that of traditional fermentation. Among 53 key aroma compounds (OAV ≥ 1), dimethyl trisulfide and trimethylpyrazine serve as critical differential markers, with flavor divergence driven by Strecker degradation, lipid peroxidation, and Maillard reaction pathways. EEG theta/alpha power analysis confirms that UPI and UIR elicit olfactory pleasantness responses resembling traditional fermentation, establishing a multiscale framework guiding flavor-preserving sterilization.

papers.title: Beyond dream enactment: Pharmacological effects on REM atonia in REM sleep behavior disorder - a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Pharmacological treatments for REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) aim to reduce injurious dream enactment, but their effects on the underlying loss of REM atonia remain uncertain. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, CENTRAL, and trial registries through October 15, 2026 for studies reporting quantitative REM sleep without atonia (RSWA) during pharmacological treatment of adults with isolated RBD or RBD associated with a clinically manifest synucleinopathy. Screening and methodological assessments were reconciled by two reviewers. Risk of bias and certainty were evaluated using design-appropriate tools. Findings were synthesized by drug and RSWA component without meta-analysis because comparable effect estimates were insufficient. Seventeen reports representing 16 independent studies were included: three randomized trials, 11 nonrandomized longitudinal studies, and two cross-sectional studies. Clonazepam was associated with variable changes in phasic and tonic EMG activity, without conclusive evidence of consistent improvement in quantitative REM atonia. Melatonin studies suggested possible improvements in some RSWA measures, whereas dopaminergic treatment frequently improved clinical symptoms without significant RSWA change. No randomized comparison demonstrated clear superiority for quantitative RSWA. Small samples, heterogeneous scoring, and incomplete comparative data limited certainty. Current evidence does not establish consistent pharmacological improvement in quantitative REM atonia in RBD, despite frequently reported symptomatic benefits. This does not demonstrate the absence of physiological drug effects, given the limited precision, methodological heterogeneity, and variable emphasis placed on RSWA across studies. Clinical improvement and quantitative REM atonia should therefore remain distinct but complementary outcomes in future trials, including investigations of potential neuroprotective treatments.

papers.title: Overnight changes in Cheyne-Stokes respiratory cycle characteristics and oxygen saturation in patients with heart failure and central sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: The cycle length (CL) of Cheyne-Stokes respiration (CSR) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and central sleep apnea (CSA) relates inversely to cardiac output. CL can increase overnight. We hypothesized that a concurrent overnight increase in the duration of apnea (apnea length; AL) will cause greater dips in oxygen saturation in the second than the first half of the night. Baseline polysomnograms of all 198 ADVENT-HF participants with CSA were analyzed. The first and last 10 CSR cycles (from the start of one apnea to that of the next) in stage N2 sleep were identified. We extracted CL, AL, and lung to finger circulation time (LFCT, from the end of an apnea to the subsequent SaO2 nadir detected by finger oximetry). We examined relationships between mean values for LFCT, CL and AL over all 20 cycles and then compared mean values for CSR-related characteristics calculated for the first and second half of the night. CL and AL correlated with LFCT (r2 = 0.50, p < 0.001 and r2 = 0.23, p < 0.001, respectively). There were overnight increases in CL (54.4 ± 15.7 vs 59.1 ± 16.6 s), AL (24.5 ± 6.9 vs 27.5 ± 8.8 s) and LFCT (28.9 ± 10.6 vs 30.9 ± 10.5 s, p < 0.001 for all), whereas neither minimum nor mean SaO2 changed (89.4 ± 4.1 vs 88.8 ± 4.8, p = 0.312 and 92.9 ± 2.5 vs 92.8 ± 2.7%, p = 0.589). Breaths during hyperpnea increased from the first to the second half of the night (9.2 ± 3.8 vs 9.8 ± 3.7 breaths, p < 0.001). In patients with HFrEF and CSA, both CSR CL and AL relate to LFCT, all of which increase overnight, suggesting that changes in circulation time influence these CSR cycle characteristics. Despite an overnight increase in AL, mean and minimum SaO2 did not fall, likely due to a concurrent increase in breaths/hyperpnea. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01128816) and the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number Register (ISRCTN67500535).

papers.title: SDAT: Synergistic domain-adaptation tuning for parameter-efficient EEG analysis.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models face significant deployment barriers in clinical settings due to high computational costs and limited cross-subject generalization, restricting their utility in real-world applications. To this end, we propose the Synergistic Domain-Adaptation Tuning (SDAT) framework, which jointly addresses parameter efficiency and domain adaptation in a unified, synergistically optimized design. On the one hand, considering the potential for concentrated and repetitive attention patterns during EEG adaptation, we design the Parameter-Efficient Adaptive Fine-Tuning (PEAFT) mechanism, which combines Modified-Scale-and-Shift Feature (MSSF) tuning and Coefficient (Coeff) tuning. Specifically, MSSF mitigates feature instability caused by intra-subject non-stationarity at the projection layers, while Coeff tuning introduces learnable residual coefficients that recombine attention maps within a graph filter subspace, allowing head-specific adaptation. On the other hand, a lightweight Class-aware Domain Adaptation (CaDA) module is constructed to explicitly align feature distributions across subjects via semantic-aware cross-subject mixup and classifier-informed semantic regularization. Notably, SDAT updates only less than 10% of the parameters required by full fine-tuning, reducing the number of trainable parameters. Extensive experimental results on LaBraM, EEG-DINO, and REVE-Base, where backbone-transfer runs are available, demonstrate that SDAT outperforms full fine-tuning and state-of-the-art (SOTA) Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) baselines in the evaluated abnormality-detection, clinical-event-classification, and emotion-recognition settings.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of age-related hearing loss on neural signatures of target selection and distractor suppression.
papers.abstract: Listeners with hearing loss (HL) often report difficulties in separating relevant target sound from irrelevant distraction. These difficulties in auditory selective attention might be caused by inefficient neural mechanisms underlying target selection and distractor suppression. In this registered report, we tested whether neural and behavioural signatures of target selection and distractor suppression were selectively impaired in 30 older listeners with HL, compared to 32 older listeners with normal hearing (NH) and 33 young NH listeners. For this purpose, we used an auditory pitch discrimination task that allowed to dissociate changes in neural alpha activity (∼8-12 Hz) and microsaccade direction in response to target selection and distractor suppression due to spatial separation. Our results show that neural signatures of spatial attention may be relatively preserved in individuals with mild-to-moderate hearing loss. Specifically, we found no conclusive evidence that hearing loss affects either target-related or distractor-related alpha lateralization. In contrast, distractor-related, but not target-related, alpha lateralization diminished with age. Furthermore, we found no conclusive evidence that single-trial alpha lateralization predicts listening accuracy or confidence. We found that attentional modulation of microsaccade rate occurred independently of directional bias and alpha lateralization. Microsaccade rate, but not microsaccade direction, was significantly increased during lateral distractor suppression compared to target selection, and we observed no oculomotor pattern mirroring neural alpha lateralization. Collectively, these findings suggest that aging more strongly affects the neural signature of distractor suppression than that of target selection.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior

papers.title: Enduring hard times: Task difficulty promotes active maintenance of response-response bindings.
papers.abstract: To form and execute action plans, we must integrate action goals, environmental features, and motor programs. Action control theories assume that this is done by temporarily binding these elements together. While such bindings dissolve shortly after action execution, they can influence subsequent actions. Usually, a full repetition of bound elements boosts, while a partial repetition impairs performance in a subsequent action episode. Notably, binding effects are reduced or fully absent in easy and overlearned tasks. Thus, it has been suggested that they depend on task involvement of prefrontal executive networks. Previously, it was unclear how task difficulty modulates the binding process. In this study, we investigated binding effects in a simple, and a difficult response-response binding paradigm, while measuring prefrontal hemodynamic activity with functional near infrared spectroscopy, and whole head electrophysiological activity with an electroencephalogram. We found larger binding effects in the difficult, compared to the simple task, both on a behavioral level and in prefrontal neural activation. Strikingly, maintenance-related α-/β-synchronization was increased between action episodes in the difficult, compared to the simple task. This increase predicted the increase in behavioral binding effects. In line with previous literature, we argue that existing long-term memory templates are insufficient for task completion in difficult tasks. Consequently, our system relies on working memory resources to flexibly maintain task-relevant information. Because working memory is prone to trial-by-trial priming by identical and trial-by-trial interference from similar memoranda, this causes the typical boost/interference pattern dependent on the overlap between subsequent action episodes observed in binding research.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior

papers.title: Associations of affective temperament and bedtime mobile phone use with purpose in life.
papers.abstract: Purpose in life (PIL) is a psychological construct that contributes toward positive well-being. This study aimed to examine the association of affective temperaments and bedtime mobile phone use with purpose in life in healthy middle-aged participants. As an opt-out study, we used the dataset of 130 participants. In the present study, we excluded 22 male subjects and focused our analysis on 108 female subjects to mitigate gender-related heterogeneity, given the significantly smaller male sample size. Multiple regression analyses using the forced entry method were conducted for PIL scores as dependent factor, with age and affective temperament scores as independent factors in model 1, adding bedtime mobile phone use as independent factor in model 2, the association was adjusted by the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) scores in model 3, finally the association was further adjusted by total sleep time and physical activity in model 4. In the final model 4, depressive temperament, irritable temperament and bedtime mobile phone use were significantly and negatively associated with PIL, whereas hyperthymic temperament was positively associated with PIL. In conclusion, these findings suggest that depressive temperament, irritable temperament and bedtime mobile phone use may be negatively associated with PIL, whereas hyperthymic temperament may be positively associated with PIL in middle-aged women.

papers.title: A narrative review of autonomic control of heart rate during sleep in typically developing children with sleep disordered breathing.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep disordered breathing (SDB) has a significant impact on cardiovascular health, primarily mediated through changes in autonomic function. Autonomic dysfunction associated with SDB can be assessed non-invasively by using heart rate variability (HRV), which reflects sympathetic and parasympathetic cardiovascular modulation. The aim of this narrative review was to summarise current evidence on HRV alterations in typically developing children with SDB and review how autonomic regulation is influenced by age, disease severity, overweight/obesity, and treatment/resolution of SDB. Twenty-six studies conducted in children and/or adolescents with SDB which assessed HRV indices were identified. Across studies, school-aged children with all severities of SDB exhibited reduced overall HRV and higher sympathovagal balance, suggesting that even primary snoring may be associated with adverse autonomic effects. In contrast, preschool children demonstrated relatively preserved or even increased vagal modulation, suggesting age-dependent effects of SDB on autonomic control. Only 3 studies have investigated the effects of overweight/obesity and these showed exacerbated autonomic dysfunction, and further studies are required. Treatment or resolution of SDB was associated with improvements in autonomic control, although findings and methodology were heterogeneous. More comprehensive and detailed studies are crucial for establishing HRV as a potential clinical biomarker to guide improved clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Emotion recognition oriented to hierarchical brain networks: A contrastive learning-driven novel dual-geometric space framework.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising tool for decoding emotional states and investigating affective disorders. However, existing EEG-based emotion recognition methods often process frequency bands separately and rely on naive feature concatenation, limiting their ability to capture complex nonlinear inter-band interactions. Furthermore, the hierarchical and non-Euclidean nature of cross-band dependencies poses challenges for learning discriminative emotion-related representations. This study aims to address these limitations by developing a hierarchical brain network framework (HBNet) for EEG-based emotion analysis. HBNet employs a dual-geometric architecture to learn hierarchical EEG representations in Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces. The Band Base Representation (BBR) branch integrates multi-layer residual self-attention with frequency-aware encoding to capture global cross-band dependencies and extract discriminative band-level features. The Band Interaction Enhancement (BIE) branch employs cross-band attention to model inter-band correlations and integrate complementary information, followed by hyperbolic mapping to characterize hierarchical cross-band relationships. Additionally, Dual-Geometric Cross-Band Contrastive Learning (DGCB-CL) is introduced to align representations across the two geometric spaces while preserving their respective geometric properties, thereby enhancing feature discrimination and generalization. Extensive experiments on public EEG emotion recognition datasets demonstrate that HBNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of the proposed dual-geometric architecture and cross-band representation learning strategy. HBNet provides a framework for modeling complex cross-band dependencies in EEG signals by integrating Euclidean and hyperbolic representations with contrastive learning. It offers a potential approach for analyzing emotion-related brain activity and may support further investigations into the neural mechanisms of affective disorders and their auxiliary assessment. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/cvmdsp/HBNet.

papers.title: Target-label-free cross-dataset monitoring detects failed motor-imagery BCI sessions.
papers.abstract: We tested whether decoder posteriors identify failed motor-imagery (MI) brain-computer interface sessions without trustworthy intent labels. The monitor is target-label-free but source-supervised: historical cohorts provide training labels; monitored sessions and cohorts do not. Each subject-specific decoder uses the participant's labelled calibration data.Approach.We analysed 38,733 trials in 190 held-out sessions from 181 participants across five public cohorts, treating participants as resampling clusters. Common spatial patterns and linear discriminant analysis (CSP-LDA) provided decoder posteriors. A nested leave-one-dataset-out ridge monitor predicted chance-normalized balanced accuracy $S$ from posterior summaries. Comparators included confidence-based estimators, normalized decoder-outputinformation $I_{\mathrm{out}}$ and cue-labelled prefix accuracy. Post hoc analyses tested command priors, class substitution, calibration and source-selected alarm cutoffs.Main results.The full monitor achieved mean absolute error 0.124 and dataset-stratified failure ($S<0.20$) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.883 (95\% confidence interval 0.826-0.930); a count-free variant achieved 0.117 and 0.872. $I_{\mathrm{out}}$ alone reached AUROC 0.877. From 20 trials, output information and labelled prefix accuracy had future-failure AUROCs of 0.852 and 0.842; non-inferiority was not established.For the full monitor without a gate, a cutoff targeting 90% source sensitivity yielded 0.932 target sensitivity and 0.644 specificity. At 90% command dominance, mean information decreased by 31.8%, AUROC changed from 0.879 to 0.861, and false alarms rose from 34 to 37. Information retained discrimination under temperature scaling but was unchanged by systematic class substitution.Significance.CSP-LDA posteriors carry session-level failure risk. Cue labels remain preferable for point estimation. Consistent transfer to Riemannian minimum-distance to-mean posteriors was not established; online and asynchronous validity remain untested.

papers.title: GRLV: Gradient reversal layer with variance loss for major depressive disorder detection.
papers.abstract: Deep learning models have been widely applied to predict major depressive disorder (MDD) using magnetoencephalography (MEG) signals. However, these models often suffer from limited performance and generalization. This is primarily due to the strong individual heterogeneity inherent in MEG temporal signals, which makes it difficult for models trained on small samples to distinguish disease-related features and individual-specific features. To address this issue, we propose GRLV, a plug-and-play framework based on gradient reversal layer with variance loss, that can be readily embedded into existing deep learning classification models. This framework introduces a variance loss function to the gradient reversal layer (GRL) framework to compensate for its convergence limitations. We evaluated GRLV on 10 backbone models, achieving an average classification accuracy of 68.2%, and surpassing baseline models by 3.5%. Visualization results prove that the GRLV framework effectively attends to bilateral occipital activities within the first 100 ms post stimulus on-set, which is associated with the early processing of negative emotional faces in MDD patients, and is a better disease marker due to less contamination from individual heterogeneity. These findings fully demonstrate the broad application potential of GRLV in existing MEG/EEG decoding models and the discovery of mental diseases. These findings fully demonstrate the broad applicability of GRLV on existing MEG/EEG decoding models and its potential for advancing the discovery of biomarkers of mental disorders.

papers.title: Stress and Work-Related Factors Among Brazilian Bank Employees.
papers.abstract: To estimate high-stress prevalence and associated factors among employees of a Brazilian public financial institution. Cross-sectional data from 90,949 employees undergoing Periodic Medical Examinations in 2019 were analyzed. Institutional Lipp classifications were dichotomized as Insignificant/Alert versus Resistance/Exhaustion. Associations were estimated using multiple logistic regression. Among 90,336 employees with stress classification, 22.2% had high stress. Higher odds were associated with female sex (OR, 1.81), low job satisfaction (OR, 2.52), low workplace comfort (OR, 1.74), continuously excessive workload (OR, 2.50), poor sleep quality (OR, 3.84), frequent sadness (OR, 2.99), little interest or pleasure (OR, 2.62), and psychiatric disorder (OR, 2.34). High stress affected approximately one fifth of employees with available classification and was associated with occupational and health-related characteristics. Cross-sectional findings do not establish temporality or causality.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine

papers.title: CFCR-Net: cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection.
papers.abstract: rConventional electroencephalography (EEG) frequency-domain analysis relies on predefined spectral bands and treats them as independent features, neglecting spectral variability and dynamic cross-band interactions. We propose a cross-frequency synergy representation paradigm and the Cross-Frequency Connectivity Reorganization Network (CFCR-Net), coupling wavelet packet sub-band decomposition with adaptive cross-frequency graph learning: orthogonalized amplitude correlation constructs a sub-band connectivity graph, and graph convolution propagates cross-frequency information. On SEED-VIG, CFCR-Net achieves 0.8831 accuracy, 0.9102 F1-score, and 75.2% leave-one-subject-out cross-subject accuracy. Visualization reveals coupling reorganizing from middle- and high-frequency toward low-frequency-dominated connectivity as fatigue develops, providing interpretable evidence of fatigue-state evolution.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering

papers.title: Mobilizing the Critically Ill: The Central Role of Nurses in Preventing ICU Complications and Enhancing Recovery.
papers.abstract: The intensive care unit (ICU) is a high-acuity environment where patients with severe illness receive comprehensive care. Immobility is common among patients with critical disease states and contributes to muscle atrophy, development of pressure ulcers, increased risk of thromboembolic events, and acute respiratory insufficiency. Similarly, delirium is another prevalent complication that further contributes to prolonged ICU stays, increased mortality, and long-term cognitive impairments. Reduced mobility, delirium, and other sequelae of critical illness pose significant challenges to patient recovery and often result in poor long-term outcomes. Early mobility has been shown to improve long-term outcomes of critically ill patients by reducing their length of hospital and ICU stay, reducing ICU-acquired weakness, improving functional outcomes, and improving long-term cognitive function. Given their direct patient contact, nurses are uniquely positioned to serve as the primary facilitators of patient mobility in the ICU. As frontline caregivers, nurses can assess a patient's readiness for mobility, monitor vital signs during activity, and provide hands-on support for safe mobilization. They are instrumental in coordinating interdisciplinary efforts, ensuring effective communication among health care team members, and advocating patient-centered mobility goals. Additionally, nurses contribute to delirium prevention and management by closely monitoring cognitive changes, facilitating family engagement, and promoting nonpharmacological interventions such as sleep hygiene and cognitive stimulation. Through their continuous presence and compassionate care, nurses not only address the physical aspects of recovery but also provide emotional support to patients and families, significantly enhancing psychological well-being in the ICU. By leveraging their clinical expertise and patient advocacy skills, nurses are essential in fostering a culture of mobility and comprehensive care in the ICU, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes and quality of life for critical illness survivors.

papers.title: Differences in Substance Use Motives by Religiosity and Parental Support Among Arab American Young Adult College Students During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
papers.abstract: Arab Americans tend to show different patterns of substance use relative to other ethnic groups, although few studies have characterized their motives for use. Because motives can confer risk for health outcomes including substance use disorders, identifying cultural values that relate to motives for use can facilitate the development of targeted interventions. Religiosity and parental support are two cultural values that can discourage using substances for varied reasons including to regulate emotion and conform with peers. The present study examined associations between religiosity, parental support, and motives for alcohol, cannabis, and tobacco product use in Arab American young adult college students. Participants (N = 125; Mage = 20.2, range 18-23; 61.9% female; 52.4% Christian upbringing, 37.3% Muslim upbringing) completed a psychosocial survey regarding religiosity, parental support, perceived changes in use during the pandemic, and motives for using alcohol, cannabis, and tobacco products. Greater religiosity was related to lower odds of using cannabis for relaxation and sleep and to higher odds of experimentation motives. In contrast, greater parental support was associated with lower odds of using alcohol for conformity and enhancement motives. Findings suggested that cultural values relate to substance use motives among Arab Americans. Given the implications of motives for problems with substance use, substance use interventions for Arab American young adult college students should be culturally-centered and address religiosity and parental support. Institutions of higher education may impact Arab American students' substance use risk by supporting resources such as cultural clubs and festivities that can cultivate these values.

papers.title: Sleep Characteristics and Sleep Problems in Vietnamese Toddlers with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: To describe sleep characteristics and sleep problems in Vietnamese toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) using the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire (BISQ) and to examine their association with autism severity. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 78 toddlers aged 18 to 36 months with ASD receiving care at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Vietnam, between August 2024 and April 2025. Caregivers completed the Vietnamese version of the BISQ. Autism severity was assessed using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition, Standard Version (CARS2-ST). The mean age of participants was 26.9 ± 5.1 months, and 80.8% were boys. Bedtime and sleep practices included high rates of screen exposure (85.9%), feeding at bedtime (82.1%), and co-sleeping (93.6%). Mean total sleep duration was 9.9 ± 1.2 hours per 24 hours, with a median sleep-onset latency of 45 minutes and frequent nocturnal awakenings. Overall, 79.5% of toddlers had at least 1 sleep problem. There was no statistically significant difference in the observed frequency of sleep problems between children with severe ASD and those with mild-moderate ASD (87.9% vs. 73.3%, p = 0.116). Sleep problems are frequently observed in Vietnamese toddlers with ASD in routine clinical care. Brief caregiver-report sleep screening may help clinicians identify sleep-related concerns early and support parent-focused guidance in developmental-behavioral pediatric practice.
papers.journal: Journal of developmental and behavioral pediatrics : JDBP

papers.title: Phosphorylation-dependent ATPase activity regulates subunit shuffling dynamics in cyanobacterial circadian clock proteins.
papers.abstract: Protein complexes are essential for cellular functions, with their dynamics increasingly recognized as key regulatory elements. In the cyanobacterial circadian clock, the KaiC hexamer is highly dynamic, undergoing phosphorylation-dependent monomer shuffling that synchronizes individual oscillators. However, the molecular mechanism of monomer shuffling is not fully understood. Here we combine a chromatography-based method with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to quantify subunit exchange in the hexamerization domain of KaiC (KaiC-CI) and in full-length KaiC. We show that ATPase activity is essential for monomer shuffling. Through quantitative modeling of experimental data, we found that adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis at two independent monomer-monomer interfaces disassembles a KaiC-CI hexamer into two oligomers. Two complementary oligomers from two different hexamers can rapidly reform a mixed hexamer. Mechanistically, ATP hydrolysis induces unstable, shuffling-competent states in hexamers, while nucleotide exchange stabilizes them, suppressing shuffling. The balance between these two processes quantitatively explains the relationship between shuffling rate and ATPase activity across KaiC mutants observed in our experiments. Applying this model to full-length KaiC revealed that phosphorylation of the KaiC-CII domain modulates shuffling primarily by affecting the nucleotide exchange rate in the CI domain. This establishes a feedback loop where CII phosphorylation alters CI ATPase activity, which in turn controls subunit exchange to synchronize CII phosphorylation across the KaiC hexamer population. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework linking ATPase-driven subunit exchange to the robustness of circadian clocks, with implications for activation-coupled dynamics in other molecular machines.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Differential sensitivities of alpha phase stability indices to temporal structure and signal-to-noise ratio: A simulation study.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalographic (EEG) phase-based measures have traditionally focused on interregional synchronization or event-locked phase alignment. However, the temporal organization of phase within a single channel and a single trial has received limited attention. In the present study, we examined whether within-trial alpha-phase organization and its temporal variability could be quantitatively characterized using single-channel EEG signals under controlled signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Simulated EEG signals were generated using mixed-frequency oscillations embedded in 1/f noise, with three conditions differing in temporal structure and six SNR levels ranging from -6 to +10 dB. Thirty simulation realizations were generated for each condition. Three indices derived from the instantaneous alpha phase were evaluated: phase concentration index (PCI), window-averaged phase concentration (WAPC), and phase concentration variability (PCV). For WAPC and PCV, sensitivity to window length was additionally examined using 100-, 250-, and 500-ms windows. The phase-based indices were also compared with conventional alpha-power decrease and increase measures. PCI showed significant overall effects of Condition and SNR, although post-hoc differences did not remain significant after correction. WAPC calculated using the 250-ms window showed greater sensitivity to condition-related differences than PCI, whereas PCV distinguished both the larger condition differences and the more subtle difference between Conditions B and C at +3 dB and above. Window length substantially affected WAPC and PCV, demonstrating that it determines the temporal scale at which phase organization and variability are characterized. Conventional alpha-power measures showed different patterns of sensitivity to Condition, suggesting that phase-based indices can characterize aspects of temporal signal organization that are not represented by power measures alone. These findings indicate that within-trial single-channel phase-based indices can quantitatively characterize distinct aspects of alpha-phase organization under controlled simulated conditions. They provide a basis for further evaluation of single-channel phase measures using empirical EEG data.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbance and Fatigue Across Pituitary Disorders - findings from a large-scale international cohort survey study - the DREAMS study.
papers.abstract: Pituitary dysfunction may impair sleep quality, mental health, and fatigue, reducing quality of life. However, systematic evaluations across different subtypes of pituitary disorders remain limited. We conducted a large survey to assess these outcomes in patients with pituitary disorders. This cross-sectional, anonymous web-based survey included adults with isolated anterior pituitary dysfunction (APD), isolated posterior pituitary dysfunction (arginine vasopressin deficiency, AVP-D), combined anterior and posterior pituitary dysfunction (PanHypo), and pituitary conditions without self-reported hormone dysfunction as the pituitary disease comparison group (PDC). Outcomes included sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index), depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-Trait), fatigue (Fatigue Severity Scale), insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index), and daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale). Higher scores indicated worse outcomes. Group comparisons were adjusted for age, sex, and number of comorbidities. Between September and November 2024, 451 patients completed the survey. Median age was 52 years (IQR, 42-60), 80% were female, and median disease duration was 7 years. Participants were classified as APD (43%), AVP-D (19%), PanHypo (27%), and PDC (12%). The most common aetiologies were pituitary tumours or cysts (62%) and idiopathic disorders (18%). Across all groups, patients demonstrated impaired sleep quality, clinically relevant anxiety, and subclinical depressive symptoms. Fatigue and insomnia levels were high in all groups, with significant differences in insomnia severity between subgroups. Sleep disturbances were also common among PDC without self-reported hormone dysfunction. Patients with pituitary disorders experience substantial impairments in sleep quality and fatigue irrespective of pituitary dysfunction subtype. Sleep disturbances in patients without reported hormone dysfunction suggest contributors beyond hormonal imbalance alone. These findings highlight the need for targeted assessment and management of sleep-related symptoms in pituitary disorders.

papers.title: The Future of Psychocardiology: From Psychosocial Risk to Mechanism-Based Care.
papers.abstract: Psychocardiology has established psychosocial factors as contributors to cardiovascular risk, symptom burden, and prognosis. Although mechanistic research is growing, causal evidence remains inconsistent. Broad constructs, cross-sectional designs, and insufficiently specified pathways still limit clinical translation and treatment selection. The future lies in mechanism-based care that identifies modifiable biological, psychological, behavioral, and social processes linking psychosocial factors and cardiovascular disease (CVD) bidirectionally. Mechanisms are temporally ordered causal processes through which changes in one factor produce changes in another; modifiable processes provide intervention targets. Advancing this framework requires mechanism-based phenotyping, temporally explicit research, repeated real-world assessment, and interventions testing target engagement and clinical benefit. Mechanism-based phenotyping identifies context-dependent profiles of interacting processes beyond diagnoses or symptom counts. Temporally explicit research distinguishes antecedents, triggers, maintaining factors, and consequences across disease stages and clinical contexts. Key opportunities include ambulatory and digital methods, experimental-medicine approaches testing causal hypotheses and target engagement, and integrated stepped-care models linking assessment to mechanism-informed treatment selection in CVD-management pathways. Psychocardiology offers a model for translating biopsychosocial theory into mechanism-based cardiovascular care. Clinical progress depends on identifying modifiable, temporally ordered mechanisms and testing whether interventions engage them. Implementation will require transdisciplinary training, clinical workflow integration, reimbursement structures, and equitable models of care.

papers.title: Structural Conditions in Health Care Systems and Cardiovascular Health After Release From Prison: Protocol for the SCHARP Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Compared with the general population, people released from prison experience a disproportionate prevalence of poor cardiovascular (CV) health, CV events, and CV mortality following release. Access to community health care services is key to preventing poor CV outcomes, yet people released from prison report barriers to accessing health care. In the Structural Conditions and Health After Release from Prison (SCHARP) study, we aim to examine how structural conditions, or the policies, procedures, and practices, within health care systems are associated with health care utilization and CV outcomes experienced by people recently released from prison. We recruited people recently released from prisons in Colorado into an observational cohort to follow their utilization outcomes over 12 months after study enrollment. Participants' CV health based on Life's Essential 8 (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, BMI, physical activity, diet, tobacco use, and sleep) was measured at enrollment. At enrollment, self-reported exposure to health care system conditions (eg, access experiences related to insurance status, use of peer navigators, experiences of health care discrimination, receipt of support for health-related social risk factors, and access to specialized services such as substance use treatment) since release were assessed. Using the Colorado All Payer Claims Database, we will next examine the association between exposure to structural conditions and primary outcomes of health care utilization (clinic visits, emergency visits, and hospitalization) and secondary outcome of CV hospitalization. This study was funded in September 2022. Between August 2023 and September 2025, we enrolled 508 participants. Data collection is expected to be completed in 2027 and data analysis in 2028. In a large prospective cohort of people released from prison, the SCHARP study will systematically measure CV health, identify exposure to structural conditions, and link these exposures to health care utilization and CV hospitalization. These findings will be used to develop and disseminate resources for health care systems interested in improving health care utilization and CV outcomes for people released from prison. ClincalTrials.gov NCT05989282; https://tinyurl.com/355ey7ez. DERR1-10.2196/105111.

papers.title: Association of sleep patterns with organ aging: a large community-based study.
papers.abstract: Sleep plays an essential role in biological processes, but its relationship with biological aging is under-explored. We examined the relationship between sleep patterns and both organ age gaps and accelerated organ aging. This study included 247,697 participants without major chronic disease, from the UK Biobank (mean age: 55.20 ± 8.09). Eight organ system-specific ages (cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic, and brain) were constructed using machine learning, incorporating biomarker, physiological, anthropometric, and neuroimaging data. Organ-specific age gaps (the difference between estimated age and chronological age) were calculated, and accelerated organ aging was defined as an organ age gap exceeding the 95th percentile. Sleep patterns were self-reported at baseline, comprising sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness, and were classified into healthy, intermediate, and poor. Having a poor compared to a healthy sleep pattern was related to significantly higher organ-specific age gaps for all but one organ (specifically pulmonary, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic, and brain), and was associated with faster pulmonary (OR 1.251, 95%CI: 1.116-1.404), hepatic (OR 1.382, 95%CI: 1.235-1.546), musculoskeletal (OR 1.708, 95%CI: 1.491-1.957), immune (OR 1.428, 95%CI: 1.292-1.579), metabolic (OR 1.659, 95%CI: 1.477-1.864), and brain (OR 1.592, 95%CI: 1.132-2.240) aging, as well as related to significantly higher likelihood of accelerated aging in multiple (≥ 2) organ systems (OR 1.463, 95%CI: 1.281-1.670). These findings demonstrate that poor sleep pattern is associated with accelerated pulmonary, hepatic, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic and brain aging, highlighting sleep health as a modifiable target for delaying biological aging.

papers.title: Circadian coding of chemosensation: a peripheral-central oscillator framework for insect olfaction and gustation.
papers.abstract: Chemical cues guide major aspects of insect life, yet their detection and behavioral relevance vary throughout the day. Although circadian regulation of insect olfaction and gustation has been increasingly reported, the mechanisms by which local sensory clocks interact with central timing and physiological-state signals remain fragmented. Here, we systematically synthesized molecular, electrophysiological, behavioral, and ecological evidence for the temporal regulation of insect chemosensation for the first time. Comparison of olfaction and gustation reveals a shared organizational principle but distinct adaptive functions: olfactory rhythms primarily align long-range chemical detection with external ecological opportunities, whereas gustatory rhythms more directly couple contact chemosensation to feeding and metabolic state. On the basis of these findings, we propose a Peripheral-Central Dual Oscillator (PCDO) framework: (i) cell-autonomous peripheral clocks are necessary; (ii) central clocks do not generate primary sensory rhythms but integrate sensory timing with physiological state, memory, and ecological context; and (iii) olfactory and gustatory modalities share conserved clock effectors but are predominantly biased toward external ecological windows and internal metabolic/feeding control, respectively. This hierarchical yet flexible organization enables insects to optimize mate searching, host detection, feeding, oviposition, and predator avoidance within species-specific temporal niches. We further emphasize that both modalities are state-dependent and can serve external or internal functions; the olfactory-gustatory contrast is therefore a difference in predominant function, with exceptions arising through distinct routes, time scales, and molecular substrates of state gating. Circadian chemosensation therefore represents a temporal computation that enables insects to determine not only which chemical signals are available but also when those signals should influence behavior.

papers.title: Valerian, chamomile, and lavender for insomnia and sleep disturbance: a narrative review of mechanisms, clinical efficacy, and safety.
papers.abstract: Synthesize the botanical, mechanistic, clinical, and safety evidence for valerian (Valeriana officinalis L.), German chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.), and lavender (Lavandula angustifolia Mill.) in adults with insomnia disorder or sleep disturbance and to link their traditional sedative and anxiolytic applications with the current pharmacological evidence. This study was designed as a narrative review and informed by a structured search of Scopus and PubMed/MEDLINE from inception to 30 June 2026, with results restricted to English-language publications. Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical practice guidelines were given priority among the 1655 records (1282 after duplicate removal), and hand searching was conducted. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was conducted; strength of evidence was summarized based on the methodological appraisals reported in the included systematic reviews. Valerian had minimal and inconsistent effects on subjective sleep quality, no consistent effects on objective sleep latency or total sleep time, and a low methodological quality evidence base. Chamomile decreased Sleep Quality scores in a small and heterogeneous sample of trials, and there were few, small, and inconsistent insomnia-specific trials. Limited evidence suggests that oral lavender oil in the form of standardized lavender oil (Silexan) influences disturbed sleep, which seems to be mediated mainly by reduced anxiety in patients with anxiety. The results are not transferable across products because of differences in preparation, dose, route of application, and study populations. The evidence did not support any of the three botanicals as an alternative to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia or guideline-based pharmacotherapy. Despite limited evidence, some botanicals are used by patients to address sleep issues and should be discussed with the patient, including benefits, product variability, and safety. Well-powered trials of chemotyped products using objective outcomes in well-defined insomnia populations and powered adverse-event monitoring are needed.

papers.title: Near-infrared transcranial photobiomodulation reduces cognitive deficits in rat model of Alzheimer's disease: the possible role of synaptic plasticity and neurotrophic factors.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline, impaired synaptic function, and depletion of neurotrophic factors. Transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) has emerged as a potential non-invasive therapeutic option. We evaluated tPBM effects on cognition, hippocampal synaptic and neurotrophic proteins, long-term potentiation (LTP), and neuronal firing in an Aβ1-42-induced rat model of AD. Male Wistar rats were allocated to six groups: control, sham, AD, and AD+tPBM at 8, 16, or 32 J/cm². Animals received 810-nm pulsed-wave tPBM for 14 days after intracerebroventricular Aβ1-42 or vehicle injection. Behavioral outcomes used n = 8/group; electrophysiology, n = 6/group; and western blotting, n = 3/group. Outcomes included open-field, T-maze, and Barnes-maze performance, CA1 fEPSP/LTP, single-unit firing, and synaptic and neurotrophic protein expression. Compared with AD, 8 J/cm² tPBM improved T-maze alternation (p = 0.0029) and Barnes-maze escape latency (p = 0.0376) and increased probe-trial target-quadrant time (p = 0.0432). Omnibus effects were large for alternation (partial η²=0.689) and target-quadrant time (partial η²=0.709). At 8 J/cm², PSD-95 (p = 0.0422), synaptophysin (p = 0.0055), Gap-43 (p = 0.0181), NGF (p = 0.0154), GDNF (p = 0.0014), and mean post-HFS fEPSP slope (p < 0.0001) increased versus AD; corresponding omnibus partial η² values were 0.715, 0.843, 0.774, 0.852, 0.874, and 0.613, respectively. Single-unit firing also increased versus AD (p = 0.0341; partial η²=0.437). The 16- and 32-J/cm² treatments were generally non-significant. Under these conditions, 8 J/cm² was the most consistently effective tPBM fluence, attenuating Aβ-associated cognitive and synaptic deficits and enhancing hippocampal plasticity. These preclinical findings support further dose-optimized, adequately powered studies.

papers.title: Occupational night shift exposure and the risk of testicular germ cell tumours in adults: a French case-control study.
papers.abstract: Testicular germ cell tumours (TGCT) are the most common type of cancer among males aged 15-49 years in France. Given that circadian disruption affects male reproductive health, we hypothesize that night-shift work is a risk factor for TGCT. We assessed exposure to night shift work using the occupational questionnaire data from the French nation-wide prospective case-control study (TESTIS) conducted between 2015 and 2018 in 20 university hospital centers in metropolitan France. The study included 454 cases diagnosed with TGCT and 670 controls. We estimated odds ratios (ORs) of TGCT along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using conditional logistic regression models. Results: Our findings do not support a strong association between night shift work and TGCT risk overall (OR 1.01, CI 0.78 - 1.31). Likewise, the number of hours worked night shift regularly per day on the average (< 8 hours OR 1.02, CI 0.66 - 1.58; ≥8 hours OR 0.95, CI 0.71-1.26), number of days worked night shift regularly per week on the average and duration of night shift employment. This is the first study to evaluate night shift work as a probable carcinogenic exposure in relation to TGCT. Our findings indicate that night shift work is not associated with an increased risk of TGCT. This first evaluation of night shift work in relation to TGCT investigates circadian disruption as a potential etiologic factor. Our findings of no increased risk contribute important evidence to the literature on night shift work.
papers.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology

papers.title: Residential Racial Segregation and Longitudinal Cardiovascular Health Among Black Adults: Life's Essential 8 in The CARDIA Study.
papers.abstract: Racial residential segregation is a structural factor associated with cardiovascular health (CVH) and may contribute to persistent cardiovascular inequities among Black adults. While prior studies link segregation to specific clinical outcomes, less is known about its longitudinal association with multidimensional CVH. We examined 10-year associations between residential segregation and CVH among Black adults during midlife. We analyzed longitudinal data from 1,080 Black participants in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study at exam years 15, 20, and 25. Racial residential segregation was measured using the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic and modeled as time-varying continuous exposure. Repeated seven-component modified Life's Essential 8 (LE8) scores, health behavior and clinical risk factor subscores were modeled as continuous outcomes using generalized estimating equations and sequential conditional mean models, adjusting for covariates. Average participants age was 39 years, 61% were women, and 63% lived in highly segregated neighborhoods. Higher segregation was most consistently associated with lower health behavior subscores (β = -0.31; 95% CI: -0.59 to -0.02). Associations with modified LE8 scores were modest and attenuated after adjustment, while clinical risk factor subscores were not consistently associated with segregation. Exploratory analysis using binary LE8 with and without sleep classification showed lower likelihood of achieving ideal CVH with higher segregation. Residential segregation was associated primarily with health behavior components of CVH during midlife among Black adults. These findings suggest that health behavior domains may be particularly relevant to understanding the association between residential segregation and CVH.
papers.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities

papers.title: Impact of Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa on Key Clinical and Patient-Reported Outcomes in Patients With Advanced Parkinson's Disease: Responder Analysis of Two Phase 3 Clinical Trials.
papers.abstract: A post hoc responder analysis was conducted to evaluate the impact of foslevodopa/foscarbidopa (LDp/CDp) on achieving meaningful responses in clinical and patient reported outcomes among people with advanced Parkinson's disease (PwaP). Data from two trials evaluating 24-h/day continuous subcutaneous LDp/CDp infusion in PwaP were included: (1) a 12-week, randomized, double-blind, phase 3 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04380142) and (2) a 52-week, open-label, multicenter study (NCT03781167). Responders were identified relative to baseline for increased "On" time without troublesome dyskinesia (ONwoTD) and reduced "Off" time using ≥ 1-h and ≥ 3-h thresholds (robust responder). Established minimal clinically important differences evaluated Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part II (MDS-UPDRS-II), Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 (PDQ-39), European Quality of Life 5-Dimensions 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L), and Parkinson's Disease Sleep Scale-2 (PDSS-2) responders. Adjusted generalized linear models compared responder proportions treated with LDp/CDp versus oral levodopa/carbidopa (LD/CD) at weeks 4 and 12, and outcomes through week 52. By week 12, a greater percentage of patients on LDp/CDp versus those on oral LD/CD experienced statistically significant (*P < 0.05) outcome improvements with 82.7%* versus 50.2% achieving 1-h reductions in "Off" time and 61.2%* versus 27.8% achieving ≥ 3-h reductions. Similarly, 83.1%* versus 48.3% of patients achieved ≥ 1-h increases in ONwoTD and 63.4%* versus 26.1% achieved ≥ 3-h increases. A greater proportion of patients on LDp/CDp achieved complete (100%) "Off" time resolution (42.7%* vs 14.4%), as well as reduced MDS-UPDRS-II (46.6%* vs 21.9%) and PDSS-2 scores (68.6%* vs 45.4%). Response rates for PDQ-39 (47.1% vs 31.9%) and EQ-5D-5L (36.8% vs 21.7%) scores were numerically higher, although differences were not statistically significant. Treatment benefits were observed as early as 4 weeks and maintained through 52 weeks. LDp/CDp may offer rapid, consistent, and meaningful reductions in motor fluctuations, nonmotor symptoms, and increased quality of life than oral LD/CD. The sustained LDp/CDp treatment benefits suggest long-term efficacy for PwaP. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers, NCT04380142, NCT03781167.

papers.title: Comprehensive spa care as a multimodal intervention for healthspan-related outcomes: A scoping review.
papers.abstract: Population ageing has increased interest in interventions that maintain function and wellbeing across the life course. This scoping review mapped evidence on spa care as a comprehensive multimodal intervention relevant to healthspan-related outcomes. A protocol was developed a priori, and database searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus on 27 May 2026 for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Adult studies focusing on spa care, balneotherapy, thermal medicine or spa rehabilitation and addressing healthy ageing, functional health, frailty-related outcomes, psychosocial, or physiological and metabolic outcomes were eligible. Ten studies were included. The evidence covered musculoskeletal function and pain, sarcopenia-related indicators, psychosocial wellbeing and sleep, selected metabolic and inflammatory markers, cardiovascular safety, and drinking cures. Several studies evaluated multicomponent spa or spa-rehabilitation programmes, whereas others examined individual spa-related components, including drinking cures or balneotherapy added to standard care. Most findings indicated short-term improvements in symptoms, function, wellbeing or selected biomarkers, but the studies were heterogeneous in population, design, intervention content and follow-up. No study directly assessed healthspan, mortality, biological age, lifespan, or long-term chronic disease incidence. The evidence therefore supports a cautious interpretation of spa care as a clinically relevant, potentially healthspan-oriented field rather than a proven longevity intervention. Future research should distinguish comprehensive spa programmes from individual components, use longer follow-up, standardised healthspan-related outcomes and detailed reporting of intervention components.

papers.title: Expanding the Reach of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia: National Dissemination of Sleep Education to Provisional Psychologists.
papers.abstract: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the gold-standard treatment for insomnia; however, it is rarely taught in graduate psychology pathways, which limits its reach. Guided by the RE-AIM framework, this study evaluated the reach and effectiveness of a sleep and CBT-I education workshop for provisional psychologists in Australia. In 2024, the Australasian Sleep Association offered a free, online sleep workshop to all provisional psychologists nationally studying a graduate psychology pathway (e.g., Master's, Doctorate or completing an internship pathway), with registrants compared to the total number of provisional psychologists registered with the Psychology Board of Australia. Pre-post assessments measured sleep and CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy to manage sleep disturbances and participants' sleep health. Results indicated that the workshop reached 10.3% of all provisional psychologists in Australia in 2024 (n = 819). Significant improvements were observed in attendees' sleep and CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy in managing sleep disturbances, and personal sleep health (all p's < 0.001). Satisfaction ratings for the workshop overall were very positive, with 88% rating the workshop as Very Good or Excellent. This study demonstrates that a free, online sleep education workshop can reach a substantial proportion of provisional psychologists in Australia and effectively improve their CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy to manage sleep disturbances, and sleep health. However, continued and expanded sleep education efforts are needed to improve the dissemination of CBT-I into psychological practice and improve mental health outcomes.

papers.title: Behavioral Cardiovascular Health Metrics in Adolescence: Evidence From a Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2022-2023 COMPASS-Québec Cohort Supporting the Relevance of Including Recreational Screen Time.
papers.abstract: The American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 defines cardiovascular health (CVH) through four behavior factors (physical activity, diet, sleep, and nicotine exposure) and four biological factors, but it excludes recreational screen time, a prevalent sedentary behavior increasingly linked to adolescent cardiometabolic risk. We examined whether adding recreational screen time to a behavioral CVH score changes population-level estimates and their sociodemographic and school-level patterning. We analyzed cross-sectional 2022 to 2023 COMPASS-Québec data from 17,882 adolescents (ages 11-19 years). The following two behavioral CVH scores were compared: a four-component score (physical activity, diet quality, sleep health, and nicotine exposure) and a five-component score that additionally included recreational screen time. Linear mixed-effects models with school random intercepts examined associations for each score with grade, gender identity, ethnicity, material deprivation, and school type. Mean behavioral CVH was 74.3 (standard deviation 19.7) for the four-component score and 64.5 (standard deviation 18.6) for the five-component score, a 9.8-point reduction when recreational screen time was included. In both models, higher grade, greater material deprivation, racialized identity, and public rural school attendance were associated with lower behavioral CVH; boys scored higher than girls, gender diverse adolescents scored lower, and students in private schools scored higher. Including recreational screen time lowered population level behavioral CVH estimates without changing the social gradients, indicating that frameworks that exclude it may underestimate adolescent vulnerability. A more behaviorally complete approach could strengthen surveillance, improve intervention targeting, and better support school-based strategies to promote CVH equitably.
papers.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine

papers.title: Atrial Fibrillation, Atrial Flutter, and Orthodromic Atrioventricular Re-Entrant Tachycardia With a Concealed Left-Sided Accessory Pathway.
papers.abstract: Accessory pathway (AP)-mediated tachycardias are a common cause of supraventricular tachycardia; however, their relationship with atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL) is often under-recognized. A 61-year-old man presented with recurrent narrow-complex tachycardia, AF, and typical AFL occurring in close temporal proximity.
