An electrophysiology study demonstrated inducible orthodromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia with eccentric retrograde atrial activation, consistent with a concealed left inferoposterior AP. The pathway was successfully ablated. At 9-month follow-up, there was no recurrence of AF, AFL, or supraventricular tachycardia. Prior studies suggest APs may facilitate atrial arrhythmogenesis. This case highlights the interplay between atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia and atrial arrhythmias and the importance of recognizing multiple mechanisms in a single patient. Concealed APs may trigger AF and AFL. Targeted ablation can eliminate multiple arrhythmias.

papers.title: Unveiling Whole Water Neurotoxicity through Sensitive Electrophysiological Functional Profiling: Beyond Conventional Morphological Metrics.
papers.abstract: Neuroactive contaminants typically coexist as complex mixtures in aquatic ecosystems, exerting deleterious effects through combined exposures. However, current assessment approaches based on morphological endpoints (e.g., neurite outgrowth) lack sufficient sensitivity to capture functional neurotoxicity of these mixtures. To address this gap, this study establishes in vitro functional neurotoxicity testing (iFNT), an ultrasensitive bioassay leveraging high-density microelectrode arrays to profile cortical network electrophysiology. Validated using reference toxicants, their mixture, and whole water samples, iFNT achieves 5- to 500-fold higher sensitivity than the neurite outgrowth assay. This heightened sensitivity enables clearer discrimination of functional phenotypes for both individual compounds at environmentally relevant concentrations (10-8 M) and whole water samples without preconcentration, providing a powerful tool for evaluating real-world neurotoxic risks. Alarmingly, conventional monitoring indicators exhibited a pronounced mismatch with iFNT profiles across wastewater treatment stages, demonstrating that seemingly acceptable routine readings masked the persistence of latent neurotoxicity. This study challenges morphology-based paradigms, revealing that accurate whole water risk assessment necessitates integrating functional biological endpoints into future monitoring frameworks.

papers.title: Decoupling Conductivity and Interfacial State in Pristine-Like Carbon Nanotube Coatings Reveals Their Distinct Contributions to Neuronal Function.
papers.abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) combine high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and nanoscale architecture, making them promising materials for neural interfaces. However, the strong coupling between CNT morphology, electrical transport, and surface chemistry has limited identification of the material properties that directly regulate neuronal function. Here, we establish an experimental strategy to disentangle morphology-dependent network transport from interfacial wettability using pristine-like CNT coatings. Multiwalled CNTs with comparable diameters but distinct lengths were reversibly functionalized, spray-coated, and thermally defunctionalized to produce homogeneous conductive networks while recovering pristine-like electrical transport and surface chemistry. Subsequent conditioning in phosphate-buffered saline substantially reduced surface hydrophobicity without detectable alteration of the graphitic CNT framework, generating coatings with comparable interfacial wettability but distinct network morphologies. Primary spinal cord neuron-glia cultures grown on these substrates were characterized by immunocytochemistry, electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. All CNT coatings supported comparable neuroglial density and network formation, whereas PBS-conditioned coatings, characterized by a more wettable interface, consistently exhibited enhanced spontaneous bursting and calcium activity compared with their untreated coatings. Across all conditions, neuronal network activity was more consistently associated with the initial interfacial state of CNT coatings, as experimentally reflected by their wetting behavior, than with CNT length or morphology-dependent electrical transport. These findings identify the initial CNT interfacial state, with wettability serving as an experimentally accessible descriptor, as a key design parameter for CNT-based neural interfaces. Furthermore, they suggest that the initial interfacial state may influence the subsequent evolution of the biomolecular layer at the cell-facing interface, thereby contributing to the modulation of neuronal function.

papers.title: Attempts to Understand and Manipulate the Orientation and Retention of Peptides Inside Nanopores Expand the Toolbox for Nanopore-Based Proteomics.
papers.abstract: Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.

papers.title: Assessment of Sleep Quality and Psychological Distress on Stroke Incidence: A Prospective Cohort Study with Inflammatory and Metabolomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: The impact of sleep and psychological distress in stroke is increasingly recognized. However, the joint effects of the two were unclear. Thus, this study aims to investigate the impact of sleep and psychological distress. 366305 participants from the UK Biobank were included. Cox proportional hazard regression models were used to assess the longitudinal associations between sleep, psychological distress and all-cause stroke (AS). The multiplication and mediation analysis were also performed to evaluate the relationship between the two exposures. Finally, we conducted mediation analyses of 177 biomarkers between sleep, psychological stress and AS to reveal the inflammatory and metabolic mechanisms. After 16-year follow-up, sleep score showed a linear inverse correlation with AS (hazard ration [HR] = 0.96, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.94-0.98, P <0.001), whereas psychological distress showed a nonlinear positive relationship with AS (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 1.05-1.09, P <0.001). The impacts of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke were similar to AS. There was no significant interaction between sleep and psychological stress in the risk of AS, but they were mutual mediating variables. We observed that C-creative protein and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, serving as shared mediating factors for sleep and psychological stress, may be involved in the occurrence of AS. Poor sleep and high psychological stress are independent risk factors for stroke, and both can contribute to stroke risk by exacerbating inflammatory responses and affecting lipid metabolism.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.abstract: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardized resource of hierarchically organized phenotypic terms used for deep phenotyping, both in research and diagnosis. In our study, we aimed to investigate how the specificity of EEG-related HPO terms may impact phenotype and gene scoring and prioritization. We compiled three HPO-based profiles, differing only in EEG terms: (a) a full profile, including all EEG-specific terms; (b) a profile containing only the non-specific EEG term ("HP:0002353" EEG abnormality); and (c) a profile without any EEG terms. We identified a total of 185 HPO terms across 33 pediatric patients with epilepsy, with a median of 2 EEG-related terms per patient. Analysis included both phenotypic and gene scoring for each profile. We observed significantly higher scores for the non-specific and no-EEG profiles in both the phenotype and combined Exomiser scores. This effect was also observed in patients whose top gene did not change. The full profile returned the shortest candidate lists, with a median of 82 genes, followed by the no-EEG profile (142 genes) and non-specific EEG (157 genes). The top-ranked gene changed in 24-55% of patients across profile comparisons, while the full-profile top gene remained within the top three in 30/33 (non-specific EEG) and 26/33 (no-EEG) patients. Our study shows that more specific EEG-related HPO terms were associated with lower phenotype and combined Exomiser scores and changed the top-ranked gene in a subset of patients. These findings suggest that EEG-related HPO terms should be curated carefully in phenotype-driven variant prioritization. HPO terms are widely used in both clinical and research settings to provide a standardized phenotype description. In this study, we examined how EEG-related HPO terms impact variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy. We found that profiles with specific EEG terms were associated with lower phenotype and gene scores compared with those without EEG terms or with non-specific EEG abnormalities. These findings suggest that the choice of EEG-related HPO terms can influence phenotype-driven prioritization results.

papers.title: Chronic cough in patients followed in Pneumology or Geriatrics settings: not the same cough.
papers.abstract: chronic cough (CC) is a highly prevalent problem; its impact in patients treated in different settings is not known Research Question: Do CC characteristics and management differ between patients attending Pneumology and Geriatrics ambulatory care facilities for CC? all patients attending 2 Pneumology and 2 Geriatrics clinics between October 2019 and July 2024 were consecutively enrolled and were compared with respect to comorbidities, drugs, CC seasonality and circadian rhythm, Leicester questionnaire (LCQ), VAS score of CC impact. 88 (mean age 73.3, SD 8.9, 67% females) and 312 (mean age 61.9, SD 15, 62.8% females) participants were enrolled in the Geriatrics and Pneumology groups, respectively. The impact of CC was greater in Pneumology, with mean LCQ total score = 14.9 (SD: 3.58) vs 17.8 (SD: 2.78). Compared to patients enrolled in Geriatrics, those enrolled in Pneumology more frequently reported worsening of cough in winter/spring and during the night. Most Geriatrics patients reported no CC-related symptoms, while dyspnea (25.3%), dizziness (5.1%), chest pain (10.2%) and vomitus (4.8%) were reported by Pneumology patients. Compared to the Pneumology population, specialist consultations were less common in the Geriatrics population; likewise, spirometry and CT scans were performed more frequently in the Pneumology than in the Geriatrics ambulatory. CC severity, as expressed by the VAS score, was directly correlated with number of comorbidities in patients attending Geriatrics clinics (Beta 0.37, 95% CI 0.105-0.634, P 0.007), but not in patients attending Pneumology clinics . CC is characterized by different profiles of severity, impact on health status and healthcare resource use, seasonality and intraday variation in patients attending Geriatrics and Pneumology clinics. Older people also showed a lower burden of diagnostic exams. Furthermore, in patients attending Geriatrics ambulatories CC severity is correlated with the number of chronic diseases as if CC did not have an autonomous impact as in their counterpart attending Pneumology ambulatories.
papers.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea and hypertension: pathophysiological links, blood pressure phenotypes and treatment effects.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and arterial hypertension frequently coexist and are linked by recurrent nocturnal cardiovascular stress. Intermittent hypoxemia, arousals and intrathoracic pressure swings promote sympathetic activation, vascular dysfunction and abnormal blood-pressure (BP) regulation. This narrative review integrates epidemiological, mechanistic and interventional evidence on the OSA-hypertension relationship based on a PubMed search (start until September 2026). Particular emphasis is placed on nocturnal hypertension, non-dipping, masked and resistant hypertension; the roles of intermittent hypoxemia, sympathetic overactivity, baroreflex, and endothelial dysfunction; and treatment effects of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), mandibular advancement devices and weight loss. Evidence from CPAP-withdrawal trials and recent meta-analyses is used to identify characteristics associated with a greater BP response to OSA treatment. The modest average BP reduction with CPAP conceals substantial heterogeneity. Treatment effects are strongest for nocturnal BP and in patients with uncontrolled BP, severe OSA and sufficient nightly treatment exposure. Future cardiovascular OSA management should move beyond the apnea-hypopnea index toward combined characterization of nocturnal physiological stress, clinical OSA phenotype, BP phenotype, and effective treatment exposure.

papers.title: Digital Biomarker of Upper-Limb Bradykinesia Severity, Progression, and Therapy Response in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Bradykinesia is central to diagnosing and monitoring Parkinson's disease (PD). Its severity is measured with ordinal clinical scales that require an expert, compress distinct motor features into one number, and show ceiling and floor effects. To develop and validate the Digital Bradykinesia Composite Score (DBCS), a measure of upper-limb bradykinesia derived from ordinary finger-tapping videos. We analyzed 3020 finger tapping videos from 656 participants (379 PD, 155 atypical parkinsonism, 33 rapid eye movement [REM] sleep behavior disorder, 79 controls, 10 other diagnoses) recorded at more than 20 sites. Computer vision extracted kinematic features, which were combined into four domains (vigor, reflecting tapping speed and amplitude; timing; irregularity; sequence effect) and the DBCS. We evaluated the DBCS against clinician ratings, levodopa and deep brain stimulation (DBS), dopamine transporter (DaT) imaging, substantia nigra free water, and 24 weeks of unsupervised home recordings. The DBCS increased with clinical severity. It improved with levodopa and with DBS, with responsiveness similar to that of the clinical rating. In patients with DBS, levodopa was associated with a further improvement in the DBCS but not in the clinical rating. Over 24 weeks of home recordings, the DBCS increased in patients and decreased slightly in controls. Higher scores were associated with lower striatal DaT binding and higher nigral free water. A composite score derived from ordinary video was associated with bradykinesia severity, treatment response, 6-month change, and markers of nigrostriatal degeneration, which supports its further evaluation for remote monitoring and as an endpoint in clinical trials. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, Electroencephalography, and Electromyography with Intracortical Electrical Stimulation in Freely Moving Mice.
papers.abstract: Simultaneously combining cellular-resolution imaging, electrical neuromodulation, and electrophysiological monitoring in freely moving mice requires a mechanically stable chronic implant and precise synchronization across recording systems. This protocol describes an integrated preparation for cortical two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, electroencephalography (EEG), and electromyography (EMG) in freely moving, tethered mice. Using the retrosplenial cortex as an example target, the protocol details fabrication and implantation of the cranial window and electrodes, viral delivery, optical field localization, installation of a detachable imaging interface, behavioral habituation, multimodal data acquisition, and stimulation-aligned calcium-signal analysis. The preparation permits repeated optical access over short- and long-term intervals and generates cellular-resolution calcium signals together with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measurements. Representative outputs include continuous multimodal session-level recordings, mouse-level population calcium responses, and paired stimulation-off and stimulation-on response measures. The workflow can be adapted to other experimentally accessible cortical targets by modifying the cranial-window location, viral injection coordinates, electrode trajectory, and implant geometry.

papers.title: Sleep in Non-Offending Parents of Children and Adolescents Exposed to Maltreatment: The Association with Parental Victimization History.
papers.abstract: Sleep among non-offending parents of children exposed to maltreatment is insufficiently described, particularly in relation to parents' own victimization histories. We described sleep characteristics and examined differences according to parental childhood maltreatment and adulthood victimization. The analytic cohort comprised 585 non-offending parents recruited through a national learning and coping center for children and adolescents with substantiated maltreatment. Childhood maltreatment was assessed with the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and adulthood victimization with items on physical violence and sexual assault. Participants were classified into four groups: no victimization, adulthood only, childhood only, and both childhood and adulthood victimization. Sleep was self-reported for weekdays and weekends, and probable insomnia was defined using an approximation of DSM-5 criteria. Continuous outcomes were analyzed with robust linear regression and probable insomnia with modified Poisson regression, adjusted for age, sex, and education. Overall, 74.0% reported childhood and/or adulthood victimization, and 28.2% had probable insomnia. Compared with parents without reported victimization, all three victimization groups had lower sleep efficiency, greater sleep deficit, more wake after sleep onset, and shorter weekend sleep duration. Probable insomnia was more prevalent in the childhood-only group (PR 1.85, 95% CI 1.09-3.14) and the combined group (PR 1.86, 95% CI 1.16-2.99). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar estimates. Non-offending parents of children exposed to maltreatment experience substantial sleep difficulties. Associations were most consistent for wake after sleep onset, sleep efficiency, and sleep deficit, and were also evident for sleep duration and probable insomnia, particularly among parents with childhood or repeated life-course victimization.

papers.title: The effect of music therapy on function in people with Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThe investigation intended to assess the effects of music therapy on functional impairments in individuals with Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism.MethodsFrom inception to 31 August 2026, the following databases were searched systematically and independently by two investigators, including China National Knowledge Infrastructure, VIP, Wanfang Data, SinoMed, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus, concerning music therapy for Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism. A meta-analysis was performed with RevMan 5.4 software. The publication bias risk was determined using funnel plots and Egger's regression test.ResultsThirty-three studies of generally good quality were included, involving 3635 patients. Music therapy significantly improved athletic function (standardized mean difference (SMD) = -0.53, 95% CI [-0.71 to -0.35], p < 0.00001), balance (SMD = 0.45, 95% CI [0.25 to 0.64], p < 0.00001) and gait (SMD = 0.59, 95% CI [0.36 to 0.83], p < 0.00001). The depression (SMD = -0.76, 95% CI [-0.92 to -0.60], p < 0.00001), anxiety (SMD = -0.59, 95% CI [-0.85 to -0.33], p < 0.00001), sleep quality (SMD = -0.76, 95% CI [-1.01 to -0.51], p < 0.00001), cognitive function (SMD = -0.90, 95% CI [ -1.20 to -0.61], p < 0.00001) and swallowing function (SMD = -1.35, 95% CI [-1.79 to -0.92], p < 0.00001) had the significant differences due to music therapy. Improvements were noted in daily living activities (SMD = 0.53, 95% CI [0.36 to 0.70], p < 0.00001) and life quality (SMD = -0.56, 95% CI [-0.83 to -0.29], p = 0.0001).ConclusionsMusic therapy is associated with improvements in functional limitations in individuals with Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism.

papers.title: Evidence appraisal of clinical practice guidelines for managing menopausal symptoms: a systematic literature review.
papers.abstract: Symptoms associated with menopause can significantly impair quality of life. Although menopausal hormone therapy remains a well-established and highly effective intervention, a wide range of nonhormone therapies are available on and off-label as options for women in whom menopausal hormone therapy is contraindicated or not preferred. Although multiple clinical guidelines address the use of menopausal hormone therapy and nonhormone therapy for managing symptoms of menopause, the consistency of the recommendations and the robustness of the supporting evidence remain uncertain. Evaluate current United States menopause treatment guidelines in the context of emerging therapies (menopausal hormone therapy and nonhormone therapy) and evolving clinical practice. We systematically searched PubMed and EMBASE for United States menopause treatment guidelines published between 2014 and 2024. We included clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements, excluding those limited to surgically induced menopause. We extracted data using the Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcomes, Recommendation framework and assessed guideline quality. Of 655 records screened, 13 met the inclusion criteria from organizations including the American Association of Clinical Endocrinology, The Menopause Society, and the Endocrine Society. Guidelines evaluated menopausal hormone therapy for managing vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome, premature ovarian insufficiency, hypoactive sexual desire disorder, sleep disturbances, and depression, contingent on individual risk profiles. Nonhormone therapies, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, and fezolinetant, were supported by moderate to high-quality evidence. Most guidelines advise against over-the-counter or alternative treatments due to limited data. No guideline provided decision-support tools or therapeutic sequencing algorithms for nonhormone therapy selection. Seven guidelines were of moderate quality, four low-moderate, and two low quality with none rated high quality, primarily due to gaps in stakeholder involvement and applicability. This review highlights variable quality and consistency in United States clinical recommendations for vasomotor symptoms. Future guidelines should incorporate structured decision frameworks to guide therapy selection based on contraindications, patient preferences, and risk profiles.

papers.title: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation for obstructive sleep apnoea in adults.
papers.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: To evaluate the benefits and harms of implantable hypoglossal nerve stimulators for obstructive sleep apnoea in adults.
papers.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

papers.title: The Sleep-Aging-Motor Memory Triad: A Systematic Review of Task-Dependent Consolidation and Neuroplasticity.
papers.abstract: Motor learning includes a set of processes linked to practice and experience that are crucial for gaining new skills and altering behavior as time progresses. Proficiency in motor skills is crucial for maintaining autonomy and enhancing quality of life in older adults. Nonetheless, recent findings indicate that age-related sleep alterations significantly impair motor memory consolidation, thus speeding up the decline of motor abilities. Within this context, motor learning depends not only on internal neural processes but also on sleep quality, especially the preservation of slow-wave and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Disruptions to these sleep stages may interfere with the neural processes necessary for the long-term consolidation of motor skills. This synthesis emphasizes the importance of recognizing the relationship among sleep, aging, and sensorimotor plasticity, while suggesting effective intervention strategies like improving sleep or specific therapies to alleviate age-related motor deficits. These findings originate from a pre-registered systematic review of 26 research articles extracted from 740 sources indexed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. We investigated these effects on motor learning and whether they vary by task type, complexity, sleep effect, and age. This review seeks to enhance our comprehension of age-suitable empirical studies on sleep-related motor memory consolidation among healthy groups by synthesizing results from various research projects.

papers.title: Evaluating the Canadian Sleep Surgery Workforce: A National Survey Study.
papers.abstract: Sleep surgery is a rapidly-evolving specialization within Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (OHNS). However, the current landscape of sleep surgery in Canada remains scattered and poorly described. Characterizing the demographics, training backgrounds, practice patterns, and perceived barriers among surgeons performing sleep surgery is important to understand the present landscape and identify factors influencing its growth. This study aimed to examine the characteristics, demographics, and barriers experienced by otolaryngologists practicing sleep surgery in Canada. Descriptive survey study. Canada. Thirty-eight otolaryngologists. A national survey was distributed through purposive sampling to all Canadian otolaryngologists members of the Canadian Society of OHNS who self-identified dedicating 10% of their clinical practices in adult sleep surgery. The primary outcome was to evaluate the demographics and workforce needs of Canadian sleep surgeons. Secondary outcomes assessed were training, practice patterns, scope of practice, career satisfaction, and retirement plans. Response rates varied per question (N = 18-38). The mean age of participants was 43.6 years, and 60.5% identified as male. 73.7% of surgeons practice in urban settings and 57.9% held academic positions. Only 2.6% completed a sleep surgery fellowship. Major identified barriers to care included limited access to sleep studies (28.9%) and a lack of operating room time (23.7%). 28.9% of respondents spent 5% or less of their time on sleep surgery. Average wait times were 9.9 months for consultations and 7.1 months for surgeries. The Canadian sleep workforce is small and primarily composed of general otolaryngologists in urban academic centers, with most dedicating small proportion of practice to adult sleep surgery. Key barriers reported included limited testing, long wait times, and operating room resource constraints, highlighting need for improved diagnostic access, resource allocation, and training opportunities to support development of this subspecialty to serve patients.
papers.journal: Journal of otolaryngology - head & neck surgery = Le Journal d'oto-rhino-laryngologie et de chirurgie cervico-faciale
keywords: surgical treatment of obstructive sleep apnea

papers.title: Integrating Inflammation, Pathway Modulation, and Circadian Clock Genes: Conventional and Phytochemical Strategies for Safer Osteoporosis Therapy.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic and silent bone disease that destroys bone microarchitecture, thereby increasing the risk of bone fracture, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Although it is usually considered a structural deficit, bone remodeling is now fundamentally dependent on the circadian clock, osteoblast cells (responsible for the formation of new bone tissues), osteoclast cells (responsible for breaking down bone tissues), and hormonal rhythms, such as cortisol, melatonin, growth hormone, and parathyroid hormones. Current treatment methods for osteoporosis do not fully restore bone quality and cause many side effects. To address these problems, recent studies have suggested that phytomolecules, as promising therapeutic candidates, can be used for treatment. The use of phytomolecules in combination with conventional treatment, in a time-sensitive manner aligned with circadian biology, is expected to be a better treatment for osteoporosis. Disturbances in the sleep-wake cycle or in neurotransmitter homeostasis dysregulate core clock genes (BMAL-1, CLOCK, PER, CRY) in bone cells, causing instability in bone turnover. Osteochronotherapy involves scheduling the intake of conventional drugs and phytochemicals in accordance with the circadian rhythms of bone cells. This chronobiological method aims to achieve the highest therapeutic efficacy and the lowest toxicity, representing an advanced approach to osteoporosis treatment. In vitro studies have shown that bioactive agents, mainly resveratrol, icariin, genistein, quercetin, and baicalein, have osteoprotective activities with multimodal actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and direct effects on RANKL/OPG, AMPK/SIRT1, ESR, NF-κB, and Wnt/β-catenin. The study highlights the importance of incorporating circadian biology into osteoporosis management. The synchronization of therapies with the biological clock can maximize efficiency, reduce adverse effects, and help develop a new approach to bone health. The results emphasize the importance of using phytochemicals as an adjunct therapy, shed light on knowledge gaps in bone remodeling, and suggest possible avenues for utilizing circadian regulation of osteoblasts and osteoclasts to enhance bone density. Furthermore, the incorporation of natural compounds with chronotherapy represents a paradigm shift toward more personalized, safer, and biologically harmonized strategies for osteoporosis therapy. These insights also highlight critical knowledge gaps in bone remodeling research, encouraging future studies to explore how circadian rhythms and neurotransmitter pathways can be leveraged to advance precision medicine in skeletal health. It is now evident that circadian rhythm serves as an important mediator for the maintenance of healthy bones because of its function in bone remodeling. In future research, emphasis must also be placed on exploring the possible differential regulation of osteoclasts and osteoblasts by various circadian rhythms and how such regulation can help enhance bone strength. The review concludes by examining the interplay among neurotransmitter pathways, circadian biology, and sleep quality in relation to conventional and phytochemical interventions.

papers.title: Diurnal Variation in Human Breast Milk: Multi-Omic Characterization and Implications for Infant Circadian Development.
papers.abstract: Components of human breast milk exhibit circadian rhythms that may convey maternal chronobiological signals to infants; however, the diurnal patterns of the milk microbiome and metabolome remain poorly characterized. A cross-sectional study was conducted to assess feeding practices and neonatal sleep patterns in 89 mother-infant dyads. Additionally, 40 breast milk samples were collected from 20 lactating women in a separate cohort at both noon and midnight. Melatonin was measured in all 40 milk samples, microbial composition and metabolites in 13 pairs samples were quantified by LC-MS and metagenomic sequencing. In univariate analysis, neonates receiving mixed feeding demonstrated shorter nocturnal sleep compared to those exclusively breastfed; however, these associations were no longer significant after adjustment for delivery mode. A total of 335,651 microbial features were shared between the noon and midnight samples. Differential abundance analysis identified 20 bacterial genera that differed significantly between the two sampling times. The midnight samples exhibited higher relative abundances of Cognataquiflexum, Segnochrobactrum, and Aquabacterium, with both time points enriched in pathways related to lipid and amino acid metabolism. The noon-midnight differences observed suggest potential implications for infant circadian development. The potential role of circadian-matched breastfeeding strategies in infant development requires further investigation.

papers.title: Altered Resting-State and White-Matter Connectivity in Autoimmune Addison's Disease: A Multimodal Study.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune Addison's disease is exhibiting adrenal cortex dysfunction and hormonal imbalance. Current hormone replacement therapies are sub-optimal and only partially mimic the normal circadian rhythm. Previous studies found altered resting-state brain network connectivity, particularly affecting the left precuneus and the orbito-frontal cortex. Both regions are considered as major neural hubs and alterations in these regions may disrupt structural and functional connectivity patterns across broader brain networks, potentially driving cognitive and mental health issues. This study analyzed functional and structural connectivity changes of the left precuneus and bilateral orbito-frontal cortex in patients with Addison's disease compared with healthy control subjects. Cohort study involving functional and structural MRI and psychological testing. Single research institute. 123 participants: 57 patients with Addison's disease (33 females), and 66 healthy controls (37 females), aged 19 to 43 years. None. Left precuneus and bilateral orbito-frontal cortex connectivity, resting-state functional MRI, diffusion-based tractography, cognitive performance, fatigue index and medication dosage. Patients showed decreased functional connectivity between the left precuneus and left insula, and between the bilateral orbito-frontal cortex and both the bilateral temporal pole and left insula. Several right-hemisphere white-matter pathways exhibited lower mean diffusivity values, suggesting microstructural anomalies. These functional and structural brain alterations showed complex correlations with cognitive scores. Addison's disease is linked to altered resting-state connectivity in key brain hubs and right-hemispheric white-matter differences, suggesting large-scale network reorganization. The cognitive implications of these changes require further investigation.
papers.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

papers.title: Repeated Music Listening Modulates Beta Band Oscillatory Activity and Autobiographical Memory in Older Adults.
papers.abstract: Music listening is increasingly used as a nonpharmacological intervention to elicit memory retrieval. Evidence suggests that listening to autobiographically salient (ABS) music (i.e., songs associated with significant people, places, events) generates distinct neural oscillatory activity compared with familiar (FAM) music (i.e., songs that are recognized but lack personal significance). We assessed the effects of a 2-week (20 min/day) ABS music-listening intervention on behavioral autobiographical memory and music-evoked oscillatory activity in 33 healthy older adults. Listening experiences documented throughout the intervention were also examined. Following the intervention, reliving and narrative coherence subscores on the Autobiographical Recollection Test increased significantly. Time-frequency analysis revealed condition-dependent modulation over time, characterized by reduced left parietal beta desynchronization in response to ABS compared to FAM music. A repeated-measures correlation revealed within-participant associations between parietal beta power during ABS music listening and reliving subscores. Reflexive thematic analysis identified four themes characterizing the listening experience: emotional responses; autobiographical reflection; active engagement; and evolving responses to ABS music over time. Together, these results suggest that a 2-week ABS music-listening intervention is associated with increases in behavioral autobiographical memory, modulations in music-evoked oscillations, and multifaceted listening experiences in older adults. These findings may inform future music-based interventions for memory disorders.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Evaluating Predictors of Tumor in Patients With Anti-GABA-B Receptor Encephalitis.
papers.abstract: Anti-GABA-B receptor encephalitis is a rare but severe autoimmune encephalitis subtype with a close association with malignancy, particularly small-cell lung cancer. This study aimed to characterize tumor-associated clinical features and identify practical warning signs for tumor occurrence in patients with anti-GABA-B receptor encephalitis. We retrospectively enrolled 66 consecutive patients diagnosed with anti-GABA-B receptor encephalitis between July 2013 and July 2025. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, cerebrospinal fluid and serum findings, neuroimaging and electroencephalographic features, tumor-screening results, treatment, and outcomes were compared between patients with and without tumors. Among 66 patients, 38 (57.6%) were diagnosed with tumors, including 36 with small-cell lung cancer. The tumor group was older (p = 0.021) and more frequently presented with sleep disorders (33/38, 86.8% vs. 18/28, 64.3%, p = 0.031), decreased consciousness (27/38, 71.1% vs. 13/28, 46.4%, p = 0.043), and hyponatremia (22/38, 57.9% vs. 9/28, 32.1%, p = 0.038). Serum paraneoplastic antibodies were more common in patients with tumors, and tumor markers including NSE (16/34, 47.1% vs 0/24, 0%, p < 0.001) and ProGRP (23/34, 67.6% vs 3/24, 12.5%, p < 0.001) were more frequently elevated. AI-assisted CT analysis provided additional support for lung cancer screening. During follow-up, patients with tumors had poorer outcomes (p < 0.001) and higher mortality (p < 0.001). Advanced age, severe clinical presentation, elevated tumor markers, and coexisting serum paraneoplastic antibodies may help identify patients who require intensive and repeated tumor screening. AI-assisted CT diagnostic techniques may further improve early lung cancer detection, but prospective validation is required.

papers.title: Natural Antioxidants in Sleep Deprivation: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Potential, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Sleep Deprivation (SD) is a condition that undermines the body's functional state and is associated with impaired cognition and immunity, dysfunction of the circulatory and metabolic systems, and circadian misalignment. These alterations are accompanied by biologic stress, neuroendocrine imbalance, oxidative stress, and inflammation, affecting both the central nervous system and peripheral organs. Owing to this dual inflammatory and oxidative nature, antioxidant-based interventions have emerged as promising complementary therapeutic approaches. This review summarizes and critically discusses the current evidence on naturally occurring antioxidant compounds and plant extracts with potential protective effects against SD-related pathophysiological alterations, with emphasis on their molecular mechanisms of action and their multifunctional pharmacological properties. Particular attention is given to their antioxidant, antiinflammatory, hypolipidemic, antidiabetic, and cytoprotective activities, as well as their ability to modulate oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling associated with SD. Overall, the available evidence suggests that natural antioxidants may attenuate the deleterious consequences of SD through pleiotropic mechanisms. However, further mechanistic studies and well-designed clinical investigations are required to establish their therapeutic value. In addition to their potential clinical applications, these compounds may provide further insight into the molecular pathways underlying SD pathology and facilitate the development of novel natural therapeutic agents.

papers.title: Hybrid coati-gozde optimization-based EEG channel selection for automated alcoholism detection.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlcohol addiction has significant physical, psychological, and social consequences, making early detection highly important for effective treatment. Electroencephalogram (EEG) provides a reliable means for such assessment; however, using a large number of EEG channels in real-time systems increases dimensionality and computational overhead.ObjectiveTo overcome this challenge, a novel hybridized optimization algorithm called COA-GOZDE is proposed to identify the optimal channel.MethodsThis research uses Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) to extract sub-band components from EEG signals. Statistical features are computed from Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) in the time domain and classification of addicted and non-addicted subjects is carried out using k-Nearest Neighbour, Random Forest and Multi-Layer Perceptron classifiers. For optimal channel selection, a hybrid optimization strategy is developed by integrating the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) with the Gozde Optimization Algorithm (GOZDE).ResultsThe proposed COA-GOZDE achieves an accuracy of 94.6% with only 14 EEG channels, representing a substantial reduction from the original 61 while maintaining classification performance. Comparative experiments with standard optimization algorithms such as GWO, HHO, WOA and COA confirm the superiority of the hybrid algorithm in both accuracy and efficiency.ConclusionCOA-GOZDE effectively minimizes channel count by 79.34% without compromising detection performance, establishing a strong contribution to EEG-based alcohol addiction identification.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

papers.title: Optimizing sleep regularity during shiftwork is important for cognitive performance, daytime sleepiness and mood.
papers.abstract: Sleep regularity is important for performance and wellbeing. Sleep regularity is underexplored in shiftworkers, a population that may struggle to maintain regular sleep timing due to unstable work hours. It is important to understand how sleep regularity relates to wellbeing and performance outcomes for shiftworkers. Using the sleep regularity index (SRI), we assessed the relationship of sleep regularity to performance and wellbeing in maritime watchstanding shiftworkers who worked two different schedules (known as "watchbills"). Active-duty sailors (N = 23, aged 25.96 ± 3.13 years, [mean ± SD]) wore an actiwatch for ~14 days while underway on the 5-hrs on/10-hrs off watchbill, and four months later for ~10 days while on the 3-hrs on/9-hrs off watchbill. The psychomotor vigilance task (PVT) was administered two to four times daily during both underway periods; the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and Profile of Mood States were administered at the end of both data collection periods. High variability in SRI score was observed for shiftworkers on the same shift of the same schedule. Higher SRI scores were associated with faster reaction times (Spearman's rho [ρ] = -0.73, p = .019) and better cognitive performance on seven other PVT metrics (all p < .05), and reduced daytime sleepiness (ρ = -0.512, p = .013) and total mood disturbance (ρ = -0.634, p = .005). The study found that sleep regularity is an important dimension of sleep to optimize during shiftwork to improve cognitive performance and reduce daytime sleepiness and mood disturbance.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society

papers.title: Before synchrony: the unresolved specificity of neural oscillations across brains.
papers.abstract: EEG hyperscanning studies frequently report inter-brain synchrony across a wide range of frequencies, topographies, and social tasks. However, the interpretation of these findings usually relies on canonical frequency bands and builds on the assumption that oscillations are stable, sustained, and comparable across individuals. Yet, single-brain electrophysiology increasingly shows that neural oscillations are shaped by 1/f aperiodic activity, with important inter- and intra-individual differences in their properties, and with some frequency bands manifesting as short transient bursts rather than sustained rhythms. These properties are rarely addressed in hyperscanning research. They also interact with standard analytical pipelines, which implicitly assume sustained oscillations at a shared frequency across partners. Drawing on recent advances in neural oscillation research, the paper argues that IBS research should move beyond descriptive reports of synchrony and instead formulate mechanistically grounded hypotheses specifying why synchrony is expected in particular frequencies and brain regions, to build interpretable accounts of inter-brain dynamics.

papers.title: Digital Anhedonia Revisited: Reward Processing and Clinical Implications.
papers.abstract: Digital anhedonia was proposed to describe diminished enjoyment of offline experiences in the context of sustained digital engagement. Its subsequent appearance in public mental health writing and scholarly discussion creates an opportunity to clarify the concept and its evidentiary requirements. This editorial revisits selected newer findings and applies established reward-processing concepts to comparisons of online and offline pleasure within the same person. Problematic social media use should not, by itself, be interpreted as evidence of anhedonia. The studies reviewed do not directly demonstrate this pattern or establish that digital engagement causes reduced offline pleasure. I propose examining four related dimensions: anticipated pleasure, willingness to expend effort, reward learning, and pleasure during participation. Clinical assessment should establish change from previous functioning and consider apathy, executive difficulty, fatigue, mood, sleep, medications, and limitations affecting access to rewarding activities. Repeated assessments in daily life could test whether a reproducible pattern exists, while behavioral tasks and selected neuroimaging studies could investigate its behavioral and neural correlates. Neural findings would require interpretation alongside subjective experience and functioning. Digital health development should prioritize recovery of participation and enjoyment in meaningful activities. Digital anhedonia remains a hypothesis whose value depends on demonstrating explanatory and clinical usefulness.

papers.title: Targeting convergent pathogenic pathways: precision nutrition and lifestyle strategies in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) exhibits rising global incidence and substantial disease burden. Limited therapeutic response and side effects of standard medications create demand for safe adjunctive management approaches. It appraises existing evidence for targeted nutritional supplementation and structured lifestyle adjustments in UC care, covering vitamin D, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) particularly butyrate, probiotics including Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) and multi-strain blends, prebiotics, synbiotics, phytochemicals, and trace elements, together with physical activity, stress management, sleep regulation and therapeutic diets. It addresses their therapeutic effects, underlying mechanisms, and clinical practicability. Such interventions act through shared pathways including immune-inflammatory modulation, ferroptosis suppression, intestinal barrier repair and gut microbiota reshaping. A notable observation is that selenium supplementation at 200 μg/d for 10 weeks achieved higher clinical improvement among patients with mild-to-moderate active UC. The intervention yielded 38% clinical remission vs. 6% in the placebo group (p = 0.014) and lowered circulating IL-17. Exploratory microbiome data indicated more prominent butyrate-related benefits in individuals with a low Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, accompanied by significant quality-of-life gains (p = 0.003) and a non-significant trend toward reduced fecal calprotectin (p = 0.09), though these subgroup outcomes await prospective verification. Variable treatment responses support biomarker-guided personalized intervention selection. Nevertheless, most supporting evidence derives conventional trials, exploratory subgroup analyses or preclinical studies rather than validated predictive stratification tools. This review synthesizes mechanistic and clinical data to build a hypothesis-driven framework for precision-oriented dietary and lifestyle adjuncts to routine UC treatment, while differentiating these strategies from established precision therapies and outlining necessary trials to translate findings into clinical practice.

papers.title: Pathological mechanisms of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline.
papers.abstract: Chronic low-grade systemic inflammation serves as a pivotal pathological link coupling unhealthy lifestyles with malignant remodeling of body composition. This review systematically constructs and elucidates the molecular mechanisms and pathological progression of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline. Upstream multidimensional lifestyle stressors-including unhealthy diets, sleep deprivation, psychological stress, and sedentary behavior-disrupt the gut barrier, endocrine barriers, and mechanical contractile strain, thereby initiating immunometabolic reprogramming and triggering systemic chronic low-grade sterile inflammation. Acting as a core pathological driver, this low-grade inflammation impairs lipid and protein homeostasis, propels lipotoxic spillover and intramyocellular fat infiltration, and ultimately leads to the progressive decline of skeletal muscle mass and function. Concurrently, age-related neuroendocrine axis decline and dwindling sex hormone levels function as endogenous amplifiers, synergistically accelerating tissue microenvironmental remodeling and body composition imbalance in a distinctly dimorphic manner (e.g., postmenopausal estrogen deficiency accelerates muscle deterioration by inducing autophagy dysfunction in muscle stem cells). A deep mechanistic parsing of the regulatory nodes within this multidimensional network provides substantial academic value for deciphering the onset and progression of lifestyle-driven chronic inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: New-Onset Seizures and Acute Renal Failure: An Atypical and Severe Sarcoidosis Presentation.
papers.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disease with highly variable clinical expression. Although pulmonary involvement predominates, extrapulmonary presentations may be severe and diagnostically challenging, particularly in the absence of typical thoracic findings. This case report describes a male in his early 30s, with mild cognitive impairment, admitted with generalized tonic-clonic seizures and encephalopathy. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and histopathological findings were retrospectively analyzed. The patient presented with a three-month history of progressive constitutional symptoms, including weight loss, insomnia, xerosis, and lower limb edema. On admission, he developed recurrent seizures requiring sedation and mechanical ventilation. Investigation revealed severe metabolic acidosis, acute kidney injury, and pancytopenia. Neuroimaging showed nonspecific white matter changes, and electroencephalogram demonstrated epileptiform activity. Thoracoabdominal computed tomography identified splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and hepatic and renal lesions, without typical pulmonary involvement. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was non-inflammatory. Further workup showed lymphocytic alveolitis with an elevated CD4/CD8 ratio and increased serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels. Renal biopsy demonstrated granulomatous interstitial nephritis, establishing the diagnosis of systemic sarcoidosis with multiorgan involvement. High-dose corticosteroid therapy resulted in rapid clinical improvement, with recovery of renal function and resolution of encephalopathy. Temporary renal replacement therapy was required. Seizures were effectively controlled with levetiracetam. This case illustrates a rare and severe presentation of sarcoidosis, in which life-threatening neurological and renal involvement occurred in the absence of classic pulmonary features. It emphasizes the need for early recognition of atypical multisystem presentations and the pivotal role of histological confirmation. Prompt immunosuppressive therapy can be life-saving and lead to significant clinical recovery.

papers.title: Cutaneous warning signs of cardiac implantable electronic device infection: a pictorial guide for clinicians.
papers.abstract: Cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) infections are potentially life-threatening complications of pacemakers, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and cardiac resynchronization therapy devices. Although fever, bacteremia, and infective endocarditis may occur, the earliest-and sometimes only-manifestations are cutaneous abnormalities overlying the generator pocket. These findings may be subtle and mistaken for postoperative changes, hematoma, contact dermatitis, mechanical irritation, or impaired wound healing. Because patients may initially present to general practitioners, internists, emergency physicians, or dermatologists, early recognition is essential. This pictorial review illustrates the spectrum of cutaneous manifestations of CIED infection, ranging from localized erythema, swelling, pain, and delayed wound healing to erosion, sinus tract formation, purulent drainage, necrosis, and hardware exposure. It also highlights practical warning signs, appropriate referral pathways, and interventions that should be avoided before specialist assessment. Infection may extend from the pocket along the intravascular leads to the bloodstream and cardiac structures, leading to bacteremia, endocarditis, sepsis, and death. Any persistent or progressive abnormality over a CIED pocket warrants prompt evaluation, whereas purulent drainage, sinus formation, or hardware exposure should be considered evidence of device infection and require urgent electrophysiology assessment, even in the absence of systemic symptoms.

papers.title: Sea-Level Polysomnography and Periodic Breathing During Acute Normobaric Hypoxia in Healthy Adults: An Exploratory Study.
papers.abstract: Acute exposure to high altitude without prior acclimatization can induce periodic breathing (PB) in healthy individuals, but practical methods for identifying susceptibility before ascent are lacking. This exploratory study examined whether sea-level polysomnography (PSG) findings were associated with PB during acute normobaric hypoxia in healthy individuals. Fifty-four healthy young adults underwent full PSG at sea level and again under normobaric hypoxia after the chamber was set to a nominal simulated altitude of 3500 m; the device-reported oxygen fraction was 13.49% (approximately equivalent to 3300-3350 m under standard-atmosphere oxygen partial-pressure matching). According to hypoxic PSG findings, participants were classified as non-sleep-disordered breathing (non-SDB), SDB without PB, or SDB with PB. Sea-level PSG variables were then compared among groups. During acute normobaric hypoxia, 20 participants remained in the non-SDB group, 23 developed SDB without PB, and 11 developed SDB with PB. At sea level, the oxygen desaturation index (ODI), apnea-hypopnea index, non-rapid eye movement apnea-hypopnea index, average oxygen saturation during non-rapid eye movement sleep, and lowest oxygen saturation differed significantly among groups. In multivariable analysis, sea-level ODI was independently associated with PB during hypoxia. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that sea-level ODI had moderate discriminatory ability for PB, with an area under the curve of 0.798 (stratified-bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.653-0.920; DeLong P<0.001). At a cutoff of 1.15 events/h, sensitivity was 81.8% and specificity was 79.1%. In this exploratory study, sea-level ODI was associated with PB during acute normobaric hypoxia and may help identify individuals susceptible to hypoxia-related PB. Validation in larger, more sex-balanced cohorts is needed.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm regulates immune cell function and participates in the development and progression of metabolic diseases.
papers.abstract: The circadian rhythm is an intrinsic ~24-hour timing system that plays a crucial role in regulating immune functions and maintaining metabolic homeostasis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how the circadian clock influences five key immune cell types-macrophages, dendritic cells, B cells, T cells, and natural killer cells-affecting processes such as phagocytosis, antigen presentation, cytokine secretion, cell migration, antibody production, and cytotoxicity, along with their underlying molecular mechanisms. This review also examines the effects of circadian disruption on metabolic disorders-including obesity, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, and atherosclerosis-mediated by immune cell pathways. Key mechanisms include adipose tissue macrophage polarization, rhythmic IL-17A secretion by γδ T cells, and the temporal regulation of the Th17/Treg cell balance. Additionally, we address current challenges in fully elucidating these mechanisms and translating them into clinical applications, emphasizing promising avenues such as multi-omics integration, biomarker identification, and chrono-immunotherapy, while noting that the latter remains supported primarily by retrospective and hypothesis-generating evidence. Overall, this review seeks to provide a comprehensive framework for the emerging field of circadian immunometabolism and to facilitate the development of time-based precision strategies for managing metabolic diseases.

papers.title: The prevalence of nightmares in pediatric oncology: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: This scoping review aims to map the existing literature on the prevalence of nightmares in pediatric oncology patients. Nightmares are common in children and may be exacerbated by the trauma of cancer diagnosis and treatment. However, their prevalence and impact in pediatric oncology remain poorly understood. A comprehensive search was conducted in the following databases: CINAHL, PsycINFO, Embase, and MEDLINE, including grey literature. Articles were included if there was a report of nightmare prevalence in children aged 2-17 with a cancer diagnosis. Of 546 articles identified, three met the inclusion criteria. The three included studies reported nightmare prevalence ranging from 16.9 to 51% among pediatric oncology patients. Preliminary evidence suggests a heightened prevalence of nightmares in children with cancer. There is a critical need for validated nightmare-specific assessment tools and further research to distinguish between idiopathic and trauma-related nightmares. Addressing this gap is essential for improving sleep health and overall quality of life in pediatric cancer patients/survivors.

papers.title: Association between depressive symptoms and health-related quality of life among older adults with hypertension living alone.
papers.abstract: Older adults with hypertension who live alone face greater psychological pressure and poorer health outcomes compared with those living with family, yet evidence regarding the interplay of depression and quality of life in this vulnerable group remains insufficient. To determine the factors associated with depression status and health-related quality of life among older adults with hypertension living alone and to provide a reference for improving mental health and health-related quality of life in this population. Data from 278 older adults aged 65 years and older living with hypertension were selected from the "NCLM-Cohort_2023-2024 database." Depression status was assessed using the Chinese version of the Patient Health Questionnaire Depression Scale (PHQ-9), and quality of life was evaluated using the EuroQol Five-Dimension Five-Level Scale (EQ-5D-5L). Factors related to depression status and quality of life among older adults with hypertension living alone were explored using univariate analysis, binary logistic regression, and multiple linear regression. The median EuroQol Visual Analog Scale (EQ-VAS) score was 80.00 (63.75, 83.00) points. Binary logistic regression showed that female sex, sleep duration of 6-8 h or >8 h, alcohol consumption, occasional consumption of fried food, and no or very little consumption of fried food were protective factors for depression, whereas difficulty falling asleep was a risk factor for depression. Multiple linear regression indicated that marital status, occupation, sleep duration, difficulty falling asleep, and frequency of eating pickles and preserved vegetables were influencing factors for EQ-VAS scores. Depressive state significantly moderated the relationship between sleep duration and quality of life. Multiple factors are associated with depression symptoms and quality of life among older adults with hypertension living alone. Adjusting sleep duration and dietary habits, improving disease perception, and enhancing social support may help reduce the incidence of depression and improve quality of life.

papers.title: Cashew nut shell-derived N-doped biochar-UiO-66-NH2 MOF composite as a novel mesoporous adsorbent for the removal of toxic cationic dyes from water.
papers.abstract: With the increasing industrial use of synthetic dyes, their effective removal from industrial wastewater has become an important aspect of water treatment. Bio-waste-derived adsorbents have attracted considerable attention as sustainable and cost-effective materials for dye remediation. In this study, cashew nut shell-derived biochar (BC) was activated using NH4OH and subsequently integrated with amino-functionalized UiO-66-NH2 through an in situ solvothermal process to fabricate a UiO-66-NH2/BC composite. The synthesized material was systematically characterized using XRD, FTIR SEM-EDS, TEM, XPS, zeta potential analysis and BET surface area measurements to investigate its structural, morphological, surface chemical and textural properties. The composite exhibited a mesoporous structure with a specific surface area of 153.21 m2 g-1, a total pore volume of 0.1756 cm3 g-1 and an average pore diameter of 4.59 nm. Its adsorption performance was evaluated using two cationic dyes, crystal violet (CV) and methylene blue (MB), under different experimental conditions. Maximum removal efficiencies of approximately 95.8% for CV and 94.8% for MB were achieved under optimized conditions (adsorbent dosage = 0.025 g, contact time = 100 min and pH = 7). The adsorption kinetic data were well described by the pseudo-second-order model, while the equilibrium data exhibited a better fit to the Langmuir isotherm model, with maximum adsorption capacities of 210 mg g-1 for CV and 202.69 mg g-1 for MB. The mechanism of the reaction was evaluated using spectral analysis, and it was found that the primary electrostatic attraction of the functional groups, reinforced by π-π stacking, is responsible for the adsorption process. The composite demonstrated good reusability over five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, demonstrating that it is a sustainable, mechanistically well-characterized and reusable adsorbent for cationic dye-contaminated wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Are all adaptogens created equal? A comparative review and trend analysis of clinical data.
papers.abstract: The use of adaptogenic ingredients in dietary supplements and herbal medicines is increasingly common. The pharmacological effects of generally acknowledged adaptogens at tissue and cellular levels through various mechanisms result in a range of clinically relevant effects, such as increasing resilience during the stress response, supporting more rapid recovery from stressors, and decreasing the intensity of post-stress exhaustion. While clinical effects for adaptogens should be non-specific, traditional use and commercial marketing suggest different applications for individual adaptogens. To this end, the authors conducted a comparative review of clinical research to test the hypothesis based on traditional understanding that adaptogen-specific effect profiles exist and that adaptogens have differentiable clinical relevance. A comparative trend analysis of clinical evidence using accepted vote-counting methodology and data synthesis was conducted on seven generally acknowledged adaptogens: ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), schisandra (Schisandra spp.), eleuthero (Eleutherococcus senticosus), rhodiola (Rhodiola rosea), Asian ginseng (Panax ginseng), reishi (species of Ganoderma), and cordyceps (species of Cordyceps and Ophiocordyceps along with affiliated Paecilomyces hepiali). A total of 275 clinical studies were included and scored based on primary and secondary outcomes across seven clinical outcome domains: energy, cognition, mood, sleep, immunologic and inflammatory balance, cardiometabolic health, and the reproductive system. Trend analysis of this dataset identified which adaptogens showed significant positive directions of effect in each domain, and demonstrated some significant differences in clinical outcome distribution profiles for each adaptogen. Individual adaptogens show unique effect profiles measured by the outcomes of clinical research in diverse domains, corroborated by traditional use.

papers.title: Perioperative Patient-Reported Symptoms and Short-Term Recovery After Lung Cancer Surgery: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: To determine whether perioperative patient-reported symptoms provide incremental prognostic information beyond clinical and surgical characteristics for three short-term recovery outcomes after lung cancer surgery: discharge quality of recovery, prolonged postoperative stay, and 30-day readmission. This retrospective single-center longitudinal cohort included 413 adults who underwent lung cancer resection in 2023. Fifteen symptoms were rated on a 0-10 numeric rating scale at seven perioperative timepoints. Outcomes were the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at discharge, prolonged postoperative stay (longer than 7 days), and all-cause 30-day readmission. Clinical-only models were compared with symptom-augmented models that added symptoms measured before each prediction timepoint, using L2-penalized regression and repeated five-fold nested cross-validation. Discharge QoR-15 was available for 382 patients; 96 of 413 patients (23.2%) had a prolonged stay and 38 of 407 (9.3%) were readmitted. Adding postoperative day (POD) 3 symptoms increased the cross-validated R2 for discharge QoR-15 from 0.133 to 0.349; most of the increment was retained (0.171 of 0.216) when symptom domains overlapping with QoR-15 were excluded. Moderate-to-severe POD3 dyspnea, disturbed sleep, cough, and fatigue were associated with adjusted QoR-15 scores 6.8-7.8 points lower than mild symptoms; these point estimates exceeded the minimal clinically important difference. Adding POD1 symptoms increased the area under the curve (AUC) for prolonged stay from 0.679 to 0.751, and adding discharge symptoms increased the AUC for readmission from 0.616 to 0.777 in an exploratory analysis. Symptom-augmented models showed higher net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. The study was retrospective and single-center, readmission events were few, and no external validation was performed. Time-specific perioperative symptom profiles provided clinically relevant prognostic information beyond routinely available clinical and surgical characteristics. POD1, POD3, and discharge are candidate windows for symptom-informed risk updating and targeted follow-up, but prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical use.

papers.title: Mediating Effects of Psychological Resilience in Sleep Quality and Cancer-Related Fatigue in Lung Cancer Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the incidence of cancer-related fatigue (CRF) in lung cancer patients and the mediating role of psychological resilience between sleep quality and CRF. A convenience sampling method was used to select 272 lung cancer patients who received treatment in a hospital in Wuxi City between October 2023 and May 2024 as the study subjects. The research tools included a self-administered general information questionnaire, the Chinese-adapted Cancer Fatigue Scale (CFS), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Psychological Resilience Scale (CD-RISC). SPSS 26.0 was used to perform descriptive analysis, independent samples t-test, One-way ANOVA and correlation analysis on the collected data, and Bootstrap method was used to verify the mediating effect of psychological resilience between sleep quality and CRF. The incidence of CRF in 272 patients was 93.4%, and the total CFS score was 26.87 ± 5.46. Correlation analysis showed a significant negative correlation between CRF and psychological resilience (r = -0.729, P < 0.01), and a significant positive correlation with quality of sleep (r = 0.632, P < 0.01); quality of sleep and psychological resilience showed a significant negative correlation (r = -0.722, P < 0.01). Mediation analysis showed that sleep quality indirectly affected CRF through psychological resilience, and psychological resilience had a significant mediating effect between sleep quality and CRF, accounting for 75.70% of the total effect. More than 90% of lung cancer patients have cancer-related fatigue, and there is an association between sleep quality, psychological resilience, and cancer-related fatigue; future studies can use targeted psychological interventions oriented to sleep interventions to improve the psychological resilience of lung cancer patients and alleviate the adverse effects of cancer-related fatigue on patients.

papers.title: Sleep Quality as a Mediator Between Night Eating Syndrome and Quality of Life Among Lebanese University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Night eating syndrome (NES) is characterized by evening hyperphagia and nocturnal food intake and has been associated with sleep disturbance. However, its association with quality of life (QoL) among Lebanese university students remains insufficiently examined. This study's main goal is to examine the association between NES and QoL and to assess whether sleep quality statistically mediates this association. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 390 Lebanese university students between January and May 2025. Participants completed the Night Eating Diagnostic Questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and the WHOQOL-BREF. Bivariate analyses were employed to examine factors associated with QoL, then, a mediation analysis was conducted using PROCESS Macro Model 4, with sleep quality as the mediator. A possible NES was identified in 11% of participants. The mediation analysis was conducted with QoL entered as the dependent variable and sleep quality entered as the mediator. Participants with NES had significantly poorer sleep quality than those without NES. In turn, poorer sleep quality was significantly associated with lower QoL scores. The total effect of NES on QoL was statistically significant, indicating that participants with NES reported poorer QoL than those without NES. However, after accounting for sleep quality, the direct association between NES and QoL was no longer statistically significant. The indirect association of NES on QoL through sleep quality was significant. Among Lebanese university students, sleep quality statistically accounted for the association between NES and QoL in a cross-sectional mediation model. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study design does not allow causal direction to be established. Assessment of sleep quality may be useful when addressing night eating symptoms and QoL in university students.

papers.title: Noise resilience in brain decoding driven by spiking neural networks for responsive robot control.
papers.abstract: Brain computer interface (BCI) is a promising technology, expanding on many fields ranging from medical to commercial applications. The diffusion of this technique is compromised by the complexity of the treated data and the unavoidable presence of noise in those systems. This study contributes to the solution of this problem by proposing a BCI pipeline that relies on the use of spiking neural networks (SNNs), quantifying their robustness to noise in the context of brain decoding through the classification of Electroencephalography (EEG). We benchmark a shallow convolutional network against two spiking counterparts based on leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) and adaptive LIF neurons on the four-class BNCI 2014-001 motor imagery dataset. The conventional model has a slight advantage in clean conditions, but it degrades dramatically once the input is corrupted. In contrast, SNN demonstrates remarkable robustness under signal degradation. Under global Gaussian noise, CNN accuracy drops by 58.56%, whereas Adaptive LIF SNN accuracy drops by only 0.80%. Similarly, when trained on recordings with one electrode removed and tested on the complete montage, CNN loses 36.00% of its accuracy, compared with 0.34% for the SNN. With semi-simulated ocular, muscular and cardiac artifacts the gap is smaller, but the spiking models still degrade less than the CNN for every artifact type. This robustness is obtained at equal model size with 18.0 of the 24.6 MMAC required per trial by the baseline replaced by accumulate-only, spike-driven operations. Finally, the spiking model was integrated in a full decoding-to-actuation pipeline driving a Franka Emika Research 3 robot from a replayed EEG stream. These findings indicate that, compared with a dense counterpart, spiking computation substantially reduces the sensitivity of EEG decoding to signal corruption, which supports the use of SNNs in deployments where robustness matters more than peak accuracy.

papers.title: Young people at risk of suicide. Ecological momentary assessment and digital safety planning in a case series.
papers.abstract: Young people remain at high risk of recurrent suicidal behavior following a suicidal crisis, highlighting the need for innovative strategies to support post-crisis care. Digital interventions, including Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) and digital Safety Planning, may facilitate continuous monitoring and personalized support during this vulnerable period, describing the feasibility, acceptability, and clinical trajectories associated with EMA and digital Safety Planning across heterogeneous intervention exposures. We present a case series of four participants enrolled in the RCTs SmartCrisis-Teen and SmartCrisis 2.0 cohorts following a recent suicidal crisis. Clinical evolution, engagement with the digital platform, EMA data, use of the digital Safety Plan, and user satisfaction are described throughout follow-up. Clinical trajectories were heterogeneous. One participant experienced a suicide attempt during follow-up, whereas no further suicide attempts were recorded in the remaining participants. All participants remained engaged in specialized mental health care. EMA captured short-term fluctuations in suicidal ideation, sleep, and emotional functioning, although these patterns did not consistently coincide with clinical events. This case series provides preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility and acceptability of combining EMA with a digital Safety Plan as an adjunct to standard psychiatric care following a suicidal crisis. Although clinical effectiveness cannot be established from this descriptive case series, these findings support the potential clinical utility of digital monitoring and safety planning and justify further evaluation in larger prospective controlled studies.

papers.title: From acute presentation to post-discharge outcomes: intentional Z-drug versus benzodiazepine overdose in a retrospective cohort.
papers.abstract: Z-drugs are alternatives to benzodiazepines (BZDs) for insomnia, but overdose safety remains uncertain. We compared acute and post-discharge outcomes after intentional Z-drug and BZD overdose. This retrospective cohort included 239 adults (110 Z-drug; 129 BZD) treated at two emergency departments without flumazenil (2018-2024). Models adjusted for age, sex, dose category, intent, and center. Compared with BZD overdose, Z-drug overdose was associated with more recorded physical restraint use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.974; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.358-14.483), more recorded patient-behavior-related medical interruption events (PB-MIEs; aOR, 5.955; 95% CI, 2.732-12.980), and a longer emergency-department stay (adjusted median difference, 2.516 h; 95% CI, 2.056-2.845), but fewer intensive care unit (ICU) admissions (aOR, 0.092; 95% CI, 0.031-0.272). Among admitted patients, total stay was longer after Z-drug overdose (228 vs 146 h, P < 0.001). The hazard of a first documented anxiety and/or depressive diagnosis was higher after Z-drug overdose (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 2.918; 95% CI, 1.928-4.416). Recurrence proportions were similar (25.5% vs 23.3%; log-rank P = 0.426), but timing differed. The recurrence Cox model violated the proportional-hazards assumption; the adjusted HR of 1.266 is descriptive, not a constant relative risk. Among 58 recurrent cases, standard single-dose (SSD) multiples declined and documented intent shifted toward sleep-related dose escalation; this pattern may partly reflect assessment or documentation differences. Z-drug overdose was associated with more recorded behavioral-management events and a higher hazard of first documented psychiatric diagnosis, whereas BZD overdose was associated with more severe supportive-care outcomes. Initial care should integrate mental-status and respiratory monitoring with behavioral and self-harm assessment. Follow-up should address insomnia, medication safety, and mental health. Recurrence timing and intent shifts were documented associations, not causal effects.

papers.title: The smart mattress cover system for unobtrusive home sleep monitoring and automated sleep quality assessment.
